assumes: steps declare their needs (items.json) or share word stems with the earlier steps they depend on; a plain plan with no shared words reports 'no step names a need'
the dependency graph has no cycles and the goal names an existing step (otherwise refused)
greedy removal is good enough: with nested alternatives (a|b) the result is a short plan, not a proven minimum

input.shape: a step list (plan.txt, one step per line) or items.json of {name, needs:[...]} with a named goal step

name: ablation-ladder
not_for: a prose plan whose steps never repeat each other's nouns - its 'removable' list is a wording artefact, not a finding
output: the minimal plan kept toward the goal and the list of removable steps, e.g. 'minimal plan keeps 1 of 6 steps toward X; 5 removable' (--json for the full verdict)

assumes: the plan is already split into named phases, each with all four fields (abort_trigger, rollback, state_after_abort, point_of_no_return)
the vagueness test is lexical: a trigger passes if it names a number, comparison or observable, even when nothing actually measures it
a rollback's dependency on a later phase is named in its text or rollback_depends_on; a silent dependency (a backup taken later) is not seen

input.shape: a phased operation plan as JSON or a markdown table with columns phase | trigger | rollback | state after abort | ponr (optional depends)

name: abort-modes
not_for: a prose runbook with no per-phase table, or an operation already running (it checks the plan, not the world)
output: a phase table with a POINT OF NO RETURN rule plus FAIL/WARN lines (missing field, vague trigger, later-phase rollback, several or no PONR); exit 1 on any FAIL

assumes: gh, git, schtasks and python -m tv_core.writer are on PATH and answer within their timeouts (else the line reads UNKNOWN)
peers are only visible as transcripts on this PC written in the last 10 min; cloud sessions and idle-vs-thinking are invisible
a data walk over 200k files or 8 s per folder is capped, so the newest file may be later than reported

input.shape: this session's environment: the Autotrade root folder (git origin, data/ folders, writer pen, scheduled task) probed live

name: access-check
not_for: proving a push or write will succeed (REACHABLE means answered just now, not has permissions)
output: one line per probe (github, network, data, pen, peers, nightly, beyond) REACHABLE / NOT REACHABLE / UNKNOWN with evidence; --json option

assumes: each group after a split (text value, or numeric median) holds 2+ rows; with tiny groups one row decides the slope
the relation is roughly linear (least-squares slope) and conditioning on ONE attribute at a time is enough - no multivariate model
the table has attribute columns beyond x and y; with none there is no dimension to add

input.shape: rows (CSV or items JSON) with a numeric x, a numeric y and at least one extra attribute column to condition on

name: add-a-dimension
not_for: a bare time series with no extra attributes, or a causal question - a reversal says look closer, not why
output: per pair x attribute: SIMPSON REVERSAL / splits / attenuates / survives, with the pooled and per-group slopes

assumes: the marker line occurs exactly once in the file (0 or 2+ is refused)
the intended change is pure insertion: no existing line is edited, reflowed or deleted
the file uses one newline style (CRLF or LF) that the inserted block must match

input.shape: a large text file (plan, DECISIONS, memory note) plus a marker line and a block to insert; or an OLD/NEW pair of the same file

name: additions-only-splice
not_for: an edit that is meant to change or delete existing lines (a real correction), or a file whose chosen marker repeats
output: ADDITIONS_ONLY (+N lines) -> out file, or VIOLATION rows naming each old line missing or out of order; nothing written on refusal; exit 0 ok, 1 violation/marker refused, 2 bad args

assumes: the sample is long enough: a slowly mean-reverting series often fails on a short window (low power)
the series is raw, not residuals of a fitted pair (those need cointegration's stricter Engle-Granger critical values)
the tested window stands for the future: a pass on one window is no guarantee for the next

input.shape: one numeric series (a spread, ratio or feature) passed as a Python list, long enough for a lagged regression

name: adf-test
not_for: the residual spread of an OLS-fitted pair (use cointegration)
output: dict {t, crit {1%,5%,10%}, stationary_5pct, n, lags} using Dickey-Fuller critical values

assumes: each step's attack surface is recognisable from common verbs/nouns (download, store, run, measure, push, post); unusual wording reads as 'no surface named'
a verification step appears in the plan text itself after the ingest it covers (hash, compare, verify, audit)

input.shape: a pipeline or landing step list (one step per line) that ingests data, runs code or pushes changes

name: adversary-eye
not_for: code itself - it reads the plan's words and never checks whether the named checks exist in the code
output: per step: attack surface (ingest/at-rest/execute/measure/publish/message), how it could be tampered and the check that catches it, plus the FIRST UNVERIFIED INPUT step

assumes: the loader declares its allowed keys as a set literal that ast can read (or keys are passed with --keys); without a key set it exits 2
tests can be told apart as planted-fire vs quiet-on-noise from their source text
a calibration claim needs enough alert outcomes per group (--min-n, default 50) or it reports UNDERPOWERED

input.shape: an alert rules TOML plus the loader .py that holds its allowed-keys set literal and the alert test file(s); optionally an alerts JSONL with outcomes

name: alert-forge
not_for: an alert config for a different loader whose allowed keys are not a set literal, or judging whether an alert's signal has an edge
output: UNKNOWN_KEY / NO_COOLDOWN / NO_BUDGET / NO_PLANTED_FIRE / NO_QUIET_NOISE lines, test counts and VERDICT SHIP or HOLD; exit 0 SHIP, 1 HOLD, 2 bad args

assumes: a reason counts only when given inline (because, so that, to avoid, a cited Dnnn, a [REAL ...] label); reasons in other files are missed
rules are found by keywords, so descriptive sentences using always/never are counted as rules

input.shape: a prose note or plan with rule words (must, always, never, only) and repeated step verbs

name: alien-anthropologist
not_for: judging whether a rule is wrong or should be retired (it only finds unexplained ones; use retire-a-rule)
output: FIELD NOTE lines for each rule or repeated ritual stated with no reason; --json option

assumes: every size and cost is positive (the fit is OLS in log-log space)
the sizes span several multiples so the exponent is identifiable
the relation is one clean power law; a low r2 means the exponent is meaningless

input.shape: paired positive (size, cost) values spanning several multiples of size

name: allometry
not_for: data over a narrow size range or with a regime break (fits in cache, then spills) - one exponent hides the break
output: {exponent, coefficient, r2, regime sub-linear / linear / super-linear}

assumes: impact is linear and volatility constant (arithmetic Brownian motion, static schedule)
eta - gamma*tau/2 > 0 (inputs that break it are rejected)
eta and gamma are estimated from your own fills, not guessed from published values

input.shape: numeric parameters only: order size X, periods N, sigma ($/share per sqrt period), temporary impact eta, permanent impact gamma, risk aversion lambda

name: almgren-chriss
not_for: a small order that fills at once, or a cost question where square-root impact matters (use market-impact); a buy program without mirroring signs
output: holdings and trade list per period, expected cost E, variance V, objective U, kappa, half_sold_by, and a cost-vs-risk frontier over lambda against TWAP

assumes: an ID counts as explained only when followed inline by '(', '=', ':', 'is' or 'means'; a glossary elsewhere does not count
the text is short handoff prose: pronouns are only checked in the opening sentence

input.shape: a handoff, mailbox post or memory file meant for a reader who has only this text

name: amnesia
not_for: a document whose ids are deliberately defined in a linked glossary (every id will flag)
output: stand-alone score (1 minus weighted flags per sentence), the flagged pronouns, back-references, unexplained ids and assumed definites, and the amnesiac version with [?] markers

assumes: every row carries the fields the tool docstring names (label, value, source, timing); a free-text claim list is not parseable
a MEASURED row has our own measured value and an existing receipt file (checked with --root)
the target factor (default 1.8x) and the better direction of each metric are meaningful for that metric

input.shape: a CSV or JSONL of competitor/vendor claims, one row each: competitor, metric, quoted claim, source URL, label MEASURED/STATED_ONLY/NOT_MEASURABLE, value, timing method, optional ours and receipt path

name: an-scoreboard
not_for: our own results table - it grades outside claims against a target, not whether our numbers are significant
output: a markdown board (claim, label, their value, target, ours, BEAT/MISS verdict, findings) and counts; exit 1 under --strict when any finding

assumes: the weight column is non-negative and not all zero (failing columns are silently skipped)
the chosen weight is meaningful for the metric; sweeping every column as a weight is exploratory and yields curiosities
a shift in the weighted mean is read as description only; no significance is tested

input.shape: a list of items (JSON or CSV) with several numeric columns, at least one usable as a non-negative weight (capital, volume, trade count)

name: anamorphosis
not_for: a table whose only numeric columns are signed returns or Sharpes (negative weights), or a question of whether the difference is significant
output: per metric: equal-weight vs weighted mean, the shift in sd units, and the driver item holding the weight share

assumes: the first third of the text (split=0.33) holds the anchors and later numbers are estimates
enough non-date, non-year numbers exist for the log-uniform null to mean anything
units parse identically (3.4 and 3.4 Sharpe do not match)

input.shape: a forecast, target or expectation note quoting numbers early and estimating numbers later

name: anchoring-detector
not_for: texts that restate the same measured quantity twice for a real reason (closeness is not causation)
output: ANCHORED / not verdict: k/n later numbers within 25% of an early anchor vs chance rate with binomial p, the anchor that pulls hardest

assumes: energy is cheap enough to evaluate thousands of times (steps=2000 by default)
the landscape has many local optima; on a smooth unimodal one greedy mutation-forge is faster
t0 and cooling fit the energy scale - too cold freezes like greedy, too hot is a random walk

input.shape: an energy(x) function to minimise plus a neighbor(x, rng) move function over the candidate space

name: anneal
not_for: tuning a strategy on backtest data - the in-sample optimum is overfit unless guarded (walk-forward-split, pbo-overfit)
output: the best state found and its energy (anneal() result)

assumes: the cycle period is given correctly (it is not detected; phase-fold finds it)
bars are evenly spaced so k*period bars back is the same calendar point
there are enough earlier cycles; 3/3 is a thin sample, not a seasonal edge

input.shape: a CSV series of evenly spaced bars covering at least a few full cycles of a known period (12 for monthly, 5 or 7 for daily)

name: anniversary-view
not_for: testing whether a seasonal effect is real (use seasonality-test), or an irregular or gappy series
output: one line ranking this cycle's lead-in among the earlier anniversaries and what followed this point before (rose in x/y, mean change), with the cycle count

assumes: the payoff is a deterministic function of one scalar input
the shock d is the relevant volatility scale and the curvature at this center holds where it matters
a measured curvature is not tested for significance (pair with signal-nulls)

input.shape: a Python payoff function f(x) of one scalar, plus a center x and a shock size d

name: antifragile
not_for: an observed return series or backtest (it needs the payoff function, not outcomes)
output: {jensen_gap, label: antifragile | fragile | robust}

assumes: the conclusion of interest is the verdict at the LAST bar (momentum sign, trend, autocorr); it is not a backtest across time
the statistic chosen (momentum|trend|autocorr) is the one the claim actually rests on

input.shape: one numeric series (closes or returns) in a file or as a list, long enough for many window sizes

name: aperture-sweep
not_for: choosing the best lookback - picking the window that agrees after the sweep is selection; use walk-forward-split for performance over time
output: number of verdict flips across window sizes 1..N, the first flip window and the agreement share

assumes: you can make the real call yourself (network up, key in the environment); the helper only records and trims, it never calls
limits, batch sizes and feed differences measured today are dated facts that may change
one trimmed response carries no secret and is representative enough to build the parser against

input.shape: a live outside HTTP API endpoint you can call with a key, plus a list of real names/symbols from your own table

name: api-probe
not_for: an API already wrapped with fixtures and tests, or pagination and limit-cap problems (harvest-ceilings)
output: probe records (status with cause in words, bytes, seconds, seconds per name, limit headers, redacted URL), the rejected names, and one trimmed secret-scanned fixture file name

assumes: each health check is a clean boolean per component, in time order
the right patience (consecutive failures before removal) is known for how noisy the health signal is

input.shape: a stream of (component, healthy bool) health readings fed through the HealthTracker library API

name: apoptosis
not_for: deciding a single bad reading is fatal, or a health verdict that needs agreement of several checks (use quorum-sense)
output: per check: alive / ailing / apoptosis (on the removal step) / retired

assumes: both sides only APPENDED - a non-empty diff3 base section (old lines edited) is refused
the file is not a hash chain (*.chain.jsonl is refused) and not DECISIONS.md (that goes through decision-renumber)
the merge was stopped with markers present (git merge --no-commit), not resolved with -X ours/theirs

input.shape: add-only files (progress.txt, errata.md, tests.json, MAX_PROMPTS_*) holding git conflict markers in a stopped merge

name: append-only-union-resolve
not_for: a DECISIONS.md or *.chain.jsonl conflict, or a file where one side rewrote existing lines
output: RESOLVED / REFUSED per file with hunks, dropped duplicates, errata renumber map and kept_ours_where_differs; exit 0 / 1 / 2

assumes: redundancy shows as content-word overlap (>=70%); a restatement in new words is not caught
everything a newcomer needs should be introduced in this text; outside common knowledge is not known
the text has at least 2 sentences

input.shape: a handoff, how-to or plan of at least 2 sentences in plain prose

name: apprentice-master
not_for: a document for readers who share an external glossary (every shared term shows as a need)
output: master skip count, apprentice needs per 100 words, and the list of never-introduced 'the X' references, unexpanded acronyms and unitless numbers

assumes: refs were fetched: it measures origin/<branch> against origin/main as last fetched, not the live remote
the --keep paths exist at the branch tip and are the small part actually wanted
before any delete the archive tag still names the branch's current remote head (a cloud push can re-create a deleted branch)

input.shape: a git repo with a fetched remote branch of which only a few named files or folders (--keep) are wanted on main

name: archive-without-bloat
not_for: a small branch whose whole content is wanted (a plain merge is fine)
output: MERGE-OK (exit 0) or COPY+TAG (exit 3) with MB of history a merge would add vs keep size, and the copy / tag / push / ls-remote / index-row commands; exit 1 index refused, 2 bad args

assumes: the shape of interest survives mean-bucketing to the terminal width; spikes inside a bucket are hidden
a min-max (not zero-based) y axis is acceptable for the reading

input.shape: a numeric series file (one column of values, e.g. close.csv)

name: ascii-sketch
not_for: any measurement or verdict - it draws shape only and measures nothing
output: an 8-level ASCII sparkline and a fixed-height ASCII line chart with min, max and last marked

assumes: the unit is one whitespace-normalised line; a block that returns reworded is invisible and generic lines (return None, imports) give false atavisms
work merged from side branches is seen only at the first-parent merge commit
the whole patch history fits in memory (large repos need --path), and --pattern is plain enough for both git -G and Python re

input.shape: a git repository folder with first-parent history; narrow large repos with --path

name: atavism-check
not_for: a file or folder that is not a git repo, or catching a fix undone by a rewrite rather than by restoring the same lines
output: a ranked list of reborn lines with the deleting commit (sha, message) and the rebirth commit; selftest 13/13

assumes: one turn per line (long multi-paragraph turns must be pre-split)
one thread is named by one word; synonyms (vpn/tunnel) split the topic
a done word in a turn closes every topic in that turn, even unrelated ones

input.shape: a session transcript as text, one turn per line

name: attention-residue
not_for: a raw Claude Code .jsonl transcript with huge multi-line turns (units are lines)
output: topics that returned after a gap of more than `gap` units with no done word, ranked by re-mentions, with unit positions

assumes: word counts stand in for time - no timestamps are read
one topic = one recurring word; synonyms ('cache', 'rebuild') split a topic in two
the text is a conversation; a plain document lands most turns in (other)

input.shape: a conversation as 'Speaker:' lines (else paragraphs, else sentences)

name: attention-tempo
not_for: a raw .jsonl session transcript (digest it to Speaker: lines first) or mining decisions (transcript-miner)
output: per topic share of words, turns, longest run, returns; per speaker word share; attention Gini

assumes: selecting sentences is enough; nothing is rephrased
jargon is acronyms, code-style names, words with digits and a short term list
the text has 3 or more sentences

input.shape: one note or plan of 3+ sentences that several kinds of reader will see

name: audience-switch
not_for: a text that needs rewording for a novice (it only keeps or drops whole sentences)
output: three sentence cuts (novice, executive, engineer), the core kept by all, sentences only one audience gets, those every audience drops, and terms a novice needs defined

assumes: the series is smooth enough: a noisy series reads as irregular
growth has one shape over the window (a rise then fall has no single class)

input.shape: a clean growth series (counts, costs, sizes) in time order, de-noised or rolled first

name: autocatalysis
not_for: a raw noisy price series (it will read irregular; it classifies growth, not returns)
output: growth class stable | linear (slope) | exponential (autocatalytic, ratio and doubling time) | accelerating | irregular

assumes: it runs inside the C:\Autotrade workspace with gh access to issue #41 and tools/status.py present
DECISIONS.md rows carry D-numbers the parser can read; mailbox posts use the FROM/TO/TOPIC/NEEDS header
the ritual text is current (it still cites DESIGN_RULES_v2 and D75 while v3/D158+ are in force)

input.shape: the workspace's DECISIONS.md, the issue #41 comments saved to a text file, or a draft mailbox post

name: autotrade-start
not_for: a project's own CLAUDE.md ritual or a non-Autotrade repo - it reads this workspace's records only
output: a few plain lines: rules, briefing, NEEDS: Max items, last decision rows with the next free number and duplicate ids (exit 1), one-writer status

assumes: the wrapped call is idempotent; a retried non-idempotent call (an order, an append) repeats its side effect
the transient exception types are known and listed in retry_on; anything else propagates on the first call
the caller passes clock/sleep/rng when it needs deterministic tests

input.shape: a Python callable that hits a flaky resource (API pull, feed poll, download) and raises known exception types

name: backoff-retry
not_for: retrying a bug that will never succeed, or a call that places orders or writes records (not idempotent)
output: the callable's result, or the last listed exception after attempts/max_time run out, or CircuitOpenError when the breaker is open

assumes: trial_sharpes lists ALL configurations tried, per-period not annualized (missing trials overstate DSR)
gross returns are free of look-ahead and cost inputs are realistic
PBO is only checked when a time x configs candidate matrix is passed

input.shape: a backtest's gross per-period return series plus per-period Sharpes of every trial tried, costs (bps or impact inputs), optional candidate matrix

name: backtest-verdict
not_for: a single backtest with no record of the search it came from, or a request to decide whether to trade live
output: PROMOTE TO FORWARD / REJECT with failing reasons, net Sharpe, DSR, PSR, PBO, max drawdown, bootstrap mean CI, warnings

assumes: every snapshot folder carries a MANIFEST.json of relative path -> sha256
files named append-only really only grow - a legitimate rewrite shows as DIVERGES
the backups predate the suspected rewrite (a backup taken after it witnesses nothing)

input.shape: a backup root of snapshot folders, each with MANIFEST.json {relative path: sha256}, plus the live root

name: backup-witness
not_for: a live chain with no independent backup (chain-fork-guard or superposition read one history)
output: per file-snapshot INTACT / CORRUPT / ABSENT with live PREFIX_OK +N / DIVERGES at byte N / SHRUNK / GONE / SAME / CHANGED and ORDER_BREAK; exit 1 on any problem

assumes: pros and cons are signalled by cue words in its ~90-word lexicon; domain words fall off the scale
clauses split cleanly at but / however / although / semicolons
intensity words are a fair proxy for weight (crude by design)

input.shape: a decision note or plan mixing upsides and downsides in prose clauses

name: balance-scale
not_for: a quantified decision (costs and payoffs in numbers) or a jargon-heavy note where most clauses carry no cue
output: tips PRO / tips CON / balanced with the two pans, the PIVOT item whose removal flips the verdict, and the count of clauses left off the scale

assumes: hit and false-alarm rates are known and stable; rates measured in a backtest carry their own selection cost
in text mode the rates are written as percentages next to their names

input.shape: per signal a base rate, a hit rate and a false-alarm rate (JSON items, --opt values, or text with rates as percentages next to their names)

name: base-rate-view
not_for: a raw log of signal firings with no base rate or error rates (it needs the three rates)
output: P(true|flag), P(true|no flag), the naive reading's overshoot, flags per true hit and a per-1000 natural-frequency table

assumes: git fetch --prune was run first; the census itself never fetches
branches mark hold orders in commit messages (DO-NOT-LAND / NEEDS_MAX) - orders given elsewhere are invisible
the trial merge's conflict class (chain/decisions/ledger/doc/code) is decided by file path, so a misnamed ledger is treated as code

input.shape: a git repo with many remote branches to land onto a base (origin/main or origin/master)

name: batch-branch-merge
not_for: a single branch from a cloud session - use merge-cloud-branch; the census does not merge anything
output: a numbered oldest-first landing order with a policy per branch (MERGE, MERGE+UNION, NEWEST-WINS ours/theirs, REVIEW, ASK, SKIP, CONTAINED), conflicts listed, and one DECISION line per branch; read-only

assumes: a long run (more than about 10 minutes) is underway, so the questions use dead time
each open item can be classed as Max's fact, money, permission, rule or a peer's pen vs a codebase decision Claude makes itself (D69)
the items needing Max fit in one AskUserQuestion of at most 4 questions and were not already answered in MAX_PROMPTS or the ledger

input.shape: the open items of a session (ledger lines, blockers) at the moment a long run starts

name: batch-max-questions
not_for: codebase decisions Claude should make itself, or a short task with no long run to hide the wait in
output: one AskUserQuestion with the recommended option first; answers recorded verbatim; on a rejection, one plain 'what would you like to clarify?'

assumes: Flesch-Kincaid with a vowel-group syllable count is a fair difficulty proxy for this text
jargon list leans toward this workspace (trading, dev); other domains' jargon is missed
a term defined in another document still reads as undefined

input.shape: a prose note, README or reply meant for a newcomer

name: beginners-eye
not_for: checking that the text is correct (it measures difficulty only; pair expert-eye)
output: per-sentence grade with those above --opt grade flagged, glossary of terms in first-use order marked defined / NOT defined

assumes: values span several orders of magnitude from an unconstrained process
no built-in min/max, fixed digit count or narrow range (heights, dates, ids, one stock's prices)
enough values for an 8-dof chi-square at p=0.05

input.shape: a column of hundreds+ positive numbers spanning several orders of magnitude

name: benford
not_for: returns, one asset's price history or any narrow-range column - a non-conforming result there means nothing
output: {n, chi_square, conforms, observed, expected}

assumes: a bias leaves a marker phrase; bias argued in plain words leaves none
each hit is read by a person because innocent uses ('recently', 'that's why') also match
rates in the text carry a denominator when one exists (base-rate neglect is flagged structurally)

input.shape: a decision note, go/no-go verdict or keep-going argument in prose

name: bias-mirror
not_for: certifying a note bias-free from zero hits
output: per-bias hits (of 20 biases) with the sentence and the mirror move, plus the list of biases with no marker

assumes: every trade was registered with both thesis files before it opened, and the exit thesis is byte-identical (CRLF-blind) at close
the bid/ask passed are the real quotes seen then, not crossed, and --now never goes backwards
no ledger row was edited by hand (the hash chain then reads CHAIN BROKEN)

input.shape: a paper ledger JSONL written by its own register/open/close commands, plus entry- and exit-thesis text files

name: bid-ask-trade
not_for: a backtest trade list or a broker account export (it only reads ledgers it wrote)
output: report: per trade gross (mid to mid), spread paid, fees and net plus chain OK / CHAIN BROKEN (exit 1); REFUSED (exit 2) for unregistered, backdated, crossed-quote or edited-thesis actions

assumes: dependencies are plain-name calls between functions defined in the same file; method calls, imports and dynamic dispatch are invisible
for a plan, steps hand off through shared nouns; implicit hand-offs show as loose steps

input.shape: one python file (or a plan.txt step list with --kind plan)

name: birds-eye
not_for: a class-heavy or multi-module package - obj.f() calls and cross-file imports are not edges, so the map comes out nearly empty
output: nodes, edges, roots, sinks, hub and cycles, e.g. '3 nodes, 2 edges; 1 roots, 2 sinks, hub main, 0 cycles'

assumes: the covariance is well-conditioned (shrunk via cov-shrinkage, not a raw sample covariance)
views can be written as linear P/Q rows (absolute or relative) or feasible scenario functions; a view outside the scenario range raises ValueError
the market weights are an equilibrium worth starting from; the output weights are unconstrained and can go short

input.shape: a covariance matrix and market weights for N assets plus views as P rows and Q returns with confidences (or S scenario rows for entropy pooling)

name: black-litterman
not_for: a list of return guesses with no covariance or market weights, or a need for long-only capped weights out of the box
output: implied returns, posterior means, mean-variance weights; for entropy pooling the posterior probabilities q, mean, cov, KL and effective number of scenarios

assumes: the failing test ids are known from the merged tree's full output and runnable alone with pytest (or --cmd)
each ref can be checked out as a detached worktree on the same drive with disk space to spare
tests are order-independent; shared state yields NOT-REPRODUCED rather than a blame

input.shape: a repo whose merged tree has a short list of failing test ids, plus the base ref and the merged branch refs

name: blame-failure-by-branch
not_for: a whole failing suite (run per test id, one process at a time, on a 3.9 GB machine)
output: table per test x ref PASS/FAIL/ABSENT with verdict BLAME <branch> / PRE-EXISTING / INTERACTION / NOT-REPRODUCED; worktrees removed

assumes: the test command passes on an unmutated temp copy (else the run is refused)
probes print something that changes when the bad thing happens - survivors no probe notices come back UNSEEN
the repo can be copied to a temp dir and its tests rerun per mutant in tolerable time

input.shape: a repo whose tests pass, a mutants spec (or --auto FILE) and probe commands each tagged with a consequence class

name: blast-radius-mutation
not_for: a suite where you only want one kill-rate number (mutation-audit)
output: survivors ranked by worst consequence (DESTRUCTIVE 100 .. COSMETIC 1, UNSEEN) with blast score and the probe output that changed

assumes: a schema TOML describing every knob exists (written once per file kind)
the knobs live in one table named by --table
positions are meant to sit on the 1/1000 grid

input.shape: a hand-written TOML config (.blend.toml or one [table] such as alerts.toml [defaults]) plus a schema TOML of [knobs.NAME] types, ranges and required flags

name: blend-compose
not_for: row data files (use schema-contract) or a TOML for which nobody has written a schema
output: UNKNOWN_KNOB (with did-you-mean), ambiguous-value, bad-enum, out-of-range and question-line error rows, named COERCION rows, CLEAN; --emit prints the normalised table; exit 0 clean, 1 errors, 2 bad args

assumes: the module is safe to import from its path (its top level is executed)
the functions accept the sampled types (float, int, list series with NaN warm-ups)
the tolerance and samples can see a 0.1% violation, else the PASS is UNARMED

input.shape: an importable Python module of indicator or blend functions, plus a law written as a Python comparison and --var sample specs

name: blend-law
not_for: a module with side effects on import, or functions that take DataFrames
output: PASS (armed by a planted wrong law going red) / FALSIFIED with counterexample / UNARMED, or BOUNDARY lines per --knob; exit 0 / 1 / 2
probe: python {skill_dir}/blend_law.py {subject} --law "<law over the module's functions>" --var xs=series:60 --n 300

assumes: the sources describe the SAME thing, so the union of their words is meaningful
parts are content words: synonyms count as different parts and the stemmer is crude
each source is a separate block (blank-line separated or labelled)

input.shape: several partial descriptions of one thing: text blocks split by blank lines (optional 'Name:' labels), a list of strings, or items with a text field

name: blind-men-elephant
not_for: sources that disagree about the same part - it shows coverage, not truth; use rashomon for contradictions
output: the union of parts ranked by how many sources saw each, and per source its coverage share, parts only it saw and parts only it misses

assumes: the ledger marks finished asks with DONE-style words so open ones can be told apart
COMMANDS.md lists command families in the form the tool parses, and the transcript is a Claude Code .jsonl with tool_use commands
the 30 unknowns rows are filled by a person or AI afterwards; the tool fills one per finding only

input.shape: a session ledger markdown plus optional touched folders, COMMANDS.md, this session's transcript .jsonl and a sources registry

name: blind-spot-sweep
not_for: a plan document (use plan-closure) or a codebase review; it audits one session's coverage
output: five sections: open asks, loose ends (TODO/parked/UNVERIFIED with file:line), unrun command families, untouched sources, 30 unknowns with probes; exit 0 none, 1 findings, 2 bad args

assumes: both files are versions of the SAME document so sentence templates pair exactly or above --fuzz
claims live in sentences with numbers; numbers inside parentheses are treated as asides and ignored
a correction is acknowledged in the new sentence or under an Errata/Changelog/Corrections heading, not in another file

input.shape: two versions of the same prose report, receipt, README or memory file (old.md, new.md) with numbers in sentences

name: blink-comparator
not_for: comparing key=value outputs of two runs (fugue-verifier) or line diffs of code (diff-patch)
output: SILENT-CHANGE / NOTED-CHANGE / VANISHED / NEW lines with old->new values and line numbers; exit 1 on any SILENT-CHANGE

assumes: rows are pipe-table rows with a stable key in the first cell; several tables in one file are sealed as one sequence
the sidecar is stored where whoever edits the table cannot also rewrite it
the table was sealed before the change you want to detect

input.shape: a markdown pipe table with one ruling per row and its key in the first cell (DECISIONS.md)

name: blockchain-decisions
not_for: *.chain.jsonl files, which are already hash-chained (chain-fork-guard)
output: seal: sidecar hash chain; verify: EDITED / DELETED / INSERTED / REORDERED / UNSEALED / CHAIN-BROKEN rows and VERDICT INTACT (0) / TAMPERED (2)

assumes: the number of items added stays below the sized capacity n (beyond it the false-positive rate climbs)
items never need deleting or listing back
a false 'probably seen' is acceptable for the use (it must not silently drop real work)

input.shape: keys added in code from a stream, with an expected item count n and a target false-positive rate

name: bloom-filter
not_for: counting distinct items (use hyperloglog) or exact dedup where one false positive skips a real item
output: a BloomFilter object answering 'definitely not seen' / 'probably seen', union, and expected_fp_rate

assumes: rows >= background columns + 3 and the background columns are not collinear
the confounder is in the table and acts linearly (missing or nonlinear confounders leak through)

input.shape: a CSV or JSON item list with a chosen numeric pair (x, y) and other numeric background columns

name: bokeh
not_for: a small sample where you need a p-value (use hac-regression)
output: raw vs partial correlation, a verdict (relation sharpens / weakens), and the single control that moved it most; no significance test

assumes: for ci(): observations are independent; time-ordered data needs block_ci with a block longer than the autocorrelation
the sample represents the population of interest (bootstrap cannot fix a biased or selected sample)
n_for_width's sqrt(n) scaling holds only for root-n statistics on iid data

input.shape: a list of observations or returns plus a statistic function (mean, Sharpe, win rate...), called from Python

name: bootstrap-ci
not_for: the best of many tried strategies - a CI on the winner ignores the search; use deflated-sharpe / winners-curse
output: a percentile (or circular-block) confidence interval for the statistic; n_for_width returns the sample size needed for a target width

assumes: the decision is one field against one threshold; a multi-criteria rule needs one run per criterion
the band is in sd of the whole set, so a skewed field makes it too narrow on one side
the threshold defaults to the median when none is given, which may not be the real cutoff

input.shape: a list of items with one numeric field and a cutoff (or a numeric series); decision is value >= threshold

name: boundary-view
not_for: designing an anti-whipsaw dead-band (hysteresis), or a pass/fail rule that combines several fields
output: the items within the band of the line, each with its sd distance, and fragility (share of decisions that flip when the line moves one band)

assumes: the targets do not already exist on main with different bytes (any difference refuses the whole run)
the decision about WHICH paths may land was made beforehand (merge-cloud-branch, Max's words)
copying files alone is enough: history, chains and dependent files on the branch are not brought

input.shape: a repo plus a commit/branch rev and the named files or folders from it that may land

name: branch-file-copy
not_for: a file that differs on main (that is a merge question, never delete the target to force the copy)
output: BLOB_MATCH / SAME / REFUSED lines per file; exit 0 ok, 1 refused, 2 bad args, 3 blob mismatch; --dry-run writes nothing

assumes: the author wrote unfinished work into commit messages (E77 to write, NEEDS_MAX, TODO, DO NOT LAND); silent gaps are invisible
branch and base refs are fetched locally
tests.json and errata.md at the tip are in the project's formats so TESTS / ERRATUM items can be checked mechanically

input.shape: a git repo with a fetched branch and the base ref it will land on

name: branch-followup-scan
not_for: judging whether the branch's code is correct - a clean scan only means nothing self-declared is open
output: [ ] / [x] items TESTS / ERRATUM / MAX / MANUAL per commit, exit 1 if any open; dup_commits.py: DUPLICATE / SUBJECT-TWIN groups and per-branch unlanded counts

assumes: a main ref resolves (origin/main, origin/master, main, master) and remote branches are fetched
work that landed kept identical blob content; a landing with edits shows as DIFFERS
unmerged means not an ancestor of main; merged branches are not listed

input.shape: a git repo with remote branches fetched and an origin/main (or main/master) ref

name: branch-harvester
not_for: deleting branches (read-only; deletion is the D157 archive-tag step) or judging whether a DIFFERS file is better than main's
output: per branch HARVESTED or HAS_UNIQUE with ON_MAIN / IN_HISTORY / DIFFERS / MISSING counts (--show all for rows); exit 0 all harvested, 1 unique files, 2 error

assumes: the tests pass at baseline (PYTHONHASHSEED=0, TZ unset, given cwd), else it refuses
per-test results print as house PASS/FAIL lines, unittest -v or pytest -v; otherwise the whole command counts as one test
the code under test runs in the test process (a subprocess sees the unperturbed file)

input.shape: one Python module plus a targeted test command that passes on it

name: brittle-test-audit
not_for: a module whose contract promises the order a test pins (that failure is correct)
output: per harmless perturbation (reformat, noop-line, reorder-defs, rename-locals, dict-order, hashseed, tz, cwd) the tests that broke, labelled BRITTLE; exit 1 when any

assumes: generation and gate evaluation are both cheap enough to run hundreds of times
the gate is not noise-level - with a noisy gate about rate x N candidates pass by luck (a multiple-comparisons trap)
for partheno: vary() lands children near the viable region, or viable: 0 comes back

input.shape: Python callables: a generator gen_fn(rng) or an existing candidate list, plus a fertilize(candidate)->bool gate

name: broadcast-spawn
not_for: picking winning strategies on backtest noise - a high survival count there is luck, not fitness
output: {viable, spawned, fertilized, rate}; partheno.reproduce gives {variants, tried, viable}

assumes: the job takes its data folder as an argument; a job that reads paths outside the copied folder touches live files and the test is not isolated
the refusal regex matches only the guard's refusal, not clean runs (else INCONCLUSIVE)
the clean control run succeeds (else CONTROL-FAILED) and the input is a line-oriented file one canary line can join

input.shape: a job command with {ROOT} for its data folder, the real input folder and file, one canary line containing {ID}, and the guard's refusal regex

name: brood-parasite-check
not_for: a guard with no real input to copy, or a job that writes to fixed live paths it does not take as arguments
output: canary id, both return codes, fired flags, leaked output files, original_untouched and VERDICT FIRED / LEAKED / SILENT / INCONCLUSIVE / CONTROL-FAILED (exit 0/2/3/4/5)

assumes: the parent API and the bud's needs/offers are written down by hand as name sets; the tool does not read code
a declared need list is complete (hidden imports of parent internals are not detected)

input.shape: a parent's offered names (set) plus a proposed sub-tool's needs and offers sets, via the bud_off library call

name: bud
not_for: discovering the real coupling inside existing source (it only checks declared seams)
output: bud object with viable (autonomous AND minimal), missing names; reattach merges offers back

assumes: every settings.json that can install a hook is passed (user AND project), else a wired hook reads BUILT-NOT-WIRED
a log glob is given per component, else it stays WIRED-RUN-UNPROVEN
schtasks can be queried on this Windows PC (or a saved schtasks csv is given)

input.shape: a JSON list of components (name, kind, path, task, log) plus the settings.json files and the scheduler

name: built-not-wired
not_for: finding code nobody calls (vestigial)
output: per component BUILT / INSTALLED / SCHEDULED / RAN rows with proof and a verdict WIRED / BUILT-NOT-WIRED / NOT-RUN / MISSING; exit 1 unless all wired

assumes: actions are written as commands, done markers or past-tense verbs (heuristic -ed / irregular list)
plan steps share word stems with the log lines that did them
the log's claims are taken at face value; it does not prove anything was done

input.shape: a session or job log of commands, done markers and past-tense lines, optionally with a plan file via --opt plan=

name: burn-the-map
not_for: proving work was done (it reads claims; use receipt-report), or a log written in different words from the plan
output: counts of actions and intents, plan steps with no trace, and actions nobody planned

assumes: the affected parties are among its fixed nine workspace parties (Max, sessions, downstream jobs, CI, vendor terms, machine, maintainers, counterparties, readers)
a step's touch on a party shows in its verbs and keywords

input.shape: a plan or change note with action steps (land, download, schedule, post, trade)

name: bystander-eye
not_for: a plan whose affected people are outside the workspace checklist (they stay invisible)
output: per party NAMED / TOUCHED, and UNNAMED BYSTANDER findings naming the step that touches it

assumes: outcomes are resolved and independent, or clustered SEs are used when many outcomes share an event
forecasts were made before resolution (no post-resolution prices mixed in)
a bias is tradable only after spread/cost and a liquidity filter; the grader itself applies neither

input.shape: paired lists of forecast probabilities in [0,1] and realised 0/1 outcomes (prediction-market prices, model probabilities)

name: calibration-check
not_for: a single forecaster's few calls or a continuous-value forecast - it needs many binary outcomes
output: calib_slope, fls_slope (favorite-longshot), brier, brier_skill vs climatology, reliability table, n

assumes: the trap shows as a default that is a bare name or attribute chain; defaults wrapped in calls or lambdas, ALL_CAPS constants and test files are skipped
the code parses as Python
tests patch the module attribute; low-risk hits (sleep, print) must be put on --allow by hand

input.shape: a Python file or folder whose functions take injectable collaborators (getter, clock, client) as defaults

name: call-time-collaborators
not_for: code whose tests always pass the collaborator explicitly, or non-Python code
output: a list of file:line parameters whose default binds a collaborator at import time; fix pattern is None plus resolve in the body with a red-first test

assumes: input is the CUMULATIVE distinct count, not raw per-step counts or the items themselves
enough steps of baseline arrivals exist for a z=2 burst over the mean to mean something

input.shape: cumulative count of distinct types at each time step (a non-decreasing integer list)

name: cambrian
not_for: how evenly items spread across types (entropy-meter) or a level shift in a metric (changepoint)
output: dict burst, burst_steps, peak_step, peak_new, mean_arrival

assumes: the printed fractions are k/n of one common sample and carry 3+ digits
precision survives parsing (0.30 read as 0.3 lowers the detected precision)
in code, inputs appear as literal calls (open, read_csv, getenv, environ.get, argv)

input.shape: a printed result table of rates or fractions (also a report, series or code file)

name: camera-obscura
not_for: values that are not ratios of counts (Sharpe, returns) - an implied n there is meaningless
output: reconstructions of unseen inputs: implied sample size n (a lower bound), implied tick and precision, input range, file and env reads

assumes: the hard criteria (date, threshold and direction, currency, scope, action class) are parseable from the text the gate sees
hand labels exist to measure precision and recall of both stages
a human or LLM adjudicates before any irreversible act; output stays REVIEW_REQUIRED

input.shape: records from two noisy sources to link, plus hand-labelled true pairs to score generator vs generator+gate

name: candidate-then-gate
not_for: auto-acting on a high similarity score, or pairs whose deciding criteria sit only in a resolution-source body
output: candidates flagged REVIEW_REQUIRED, CONFIRMED_REVIEW / REJECTED_BY_CRITERIA with reasons; gate_eval gives precision/recall/F1 for generator alone vs with gate and lists true pairs the gate wrongly rejected

assumes: demands are known, non-negative and in one comparable unit
fair means max-min (smallest needs met in full first), not proportional or priority-weighted

input.shape: one supply number and a list of demand amounts in the same unit

name: capillary
not_for: a split that should be proportional to size or weighted by priority
output: {allocation, used, leftover, fully_met}

assumes: enough items that z-scores are stable (with 5 items one entry moves every z)
features are on comparable footing: equal-weighted Euclidean distance double-counts correlated features

input.shape: items.json or table.csv: a handful of items (strategies, skills) by several numeric features

name: caricature
not_for: deciding whether items form true groups - use speciation; this names what makes each distinct
output: each item's signature features (|z| >= min_z), nearest look-alike before and after caricature, the gap widening, and CLOSER flags when it backfires

assumes: the weight is non-negative and means importance; signed values break the area map
group detection takes the FIRST text column with repeated values, which may be the wrong one when there are several (pass group=)
it compares shares, not levels or concentration indexes

input.shape: a list of items (JSON or CSV) with a non-negative weight column (capital, volume, trades) and optionally a repeated text group column (sector)

name: cartogram
not_for: a concentration question (HHI, Gini: share-view) or a reweighted average (anamorphosis)
output: per weight: total-variation gap between count share and weight share, the most swollen and shrunken items or groups, and a text bar map

assumes: one global threshold fraction fits every node
the neighbor graph is known and complete; directions and weights are ignored

input.shape: an undirected adjacency dict {node: set(neighbors)}, seed nodes and a fractional threshold

name: cascade
not_for: plain connectivity questions with no resistance (use union-find percolate)
output: activated set, size, fraction, swept flag at the fixpoint

assumes: points are one-dimensional
bins / lo / hi are set so a real focus does not straddle a bin boundary (it splits and looks half as concentrated)
enough points that a bin's share means something

input.shape: a list of 1-D numeric endpoints or values

name: caustics
not_for: 2-D or many-dimensional clusters (gravity-cluster, k-means)
output: {counts, peak_bin, peak_range, foci, concentration}

assumes: target and branch share a merge base so base lines can be compared
the live checkout is passed with --live whenever it is involved; otherwise uncommitted appends stay hidden
the records are meant to be append-only, so any changed base line is a REWRITE

input.shape: a repo, a target ref and an incoming branch (plus the live checkout's disk via --live) holding *.chain.jsonl, DECISIONS.md, errata, progress.txt

name: chain-fork-guard
not_for: resolving a TEXT_FORK union (precommit-bundle, decision-renumber) or repairing a chain already forked on main
output: per file CHAIN_FORK / REWRITE / TEXT_FORK / ONE_SIDED; --archive writes <stem>.fork-<branch>.jsonl (never a chain); exit 1 on a fork or rewrite

assumes: rows follow tv_core's chain hash scheme with seq/kind/time_utc/body/prev/hash fields
no writer is mid-append (a torn tail line is skipped and the file reported TORN)

input.shape: a hash-chained *.chain.jsonl (seq, kind, time_utc, body, prev, hash) or a folder of them

name: chain-query
not_for: a plain JSONL log with no prev/hash fields (it reads as BROKEN)
output: per file VERIFIED / BROKEN (first bad entry and why) / TORN, then the selected rows (seq, kind, time, masked body) or counts per kind; exit 0, 3 broken or torn, 2 bad args

assumes: the commands run against a TEMP COPY with the fault already planted, never the live checkout (they run via the shell with your permissions)
the trigger edges reflect which checks should catch a downstream effect; undefined triggers are reported
the graph is big enough that k per generation is not noise

input.shape: a spec.json: seed checks plus checks {name: {cmd, triggers:[...]}} run in a temp copy of a repo with a planted fault

name: chain-reaction-fissile
not_for: whether a single test catches a bug - that is plant-the-bug; this measures spread through a check graph
output: per-generation runs/failures/DARK checks, k per generation and overall, VERDICT SUBCRITICAL/SUPERCRITICAL/CAPPED or DUD when the seed missed the plant

assumes: every step's program exists today and readers are ordered after the steps that repair their tables (preflight checks only this)
no two heavy steps can run at once on the 3.9 GB PC, and no step needs a peer session's files
the job leaves a detectable completion signal (a receipt file or a final log line) for the chain to wait on

input.shape: a long-running job (cache build, download, check_all) plus the queued steps that wait on it, as commands with what each reads and writes

name: chain-the-queue
not_for: a short task with no long job to wait on, or steps that need Max's answer before they can run
output: a self-starting chain (chain_runner or tools/nightly.py) that stops at the first non-optional failure, holds a lock and logs one JSON line per step; meanwhile new tested code instead of 'waiting'

assumes: the change is a shift in MEAN level, one break; multiple regimes need recursive splitting
noise is roughly constant so variance_reduction compares fairly
a detected break is a hypothesis, not proof; small shifts below min_detectable_shift can hide

input.shape: one numeric time series (list of floats)

name: changepoint
not_for: a change in volatility or trend slope with the same mean
output: dict index, left_mean, right_mean, variance_reduction, detected (vs min_reduction), n; min_detectable_shift floor

assumes: the snapshot was taken before the check started and T0 / T1 are known in UTC
your own records carry labels that --mine can match, so peer writes stand out
the red result is the conftest shared-chain guard, not some other error

input.shape: the shared/ folder of *.chain.jsonl chains plus the check's start and end UTC times and its log

name: check-under-concurrent-writers
not_for: a check that is red for a reason other than the shared-chain guard
output: snapshot / diff MOVED chains; window: FOREIGN and MINE records with VERDICT CONCURRENCY_ARTIFACT (4) / REAL_FAULT (5) / FOREIGN (3) / CLEAN (0)

assumes: higher values win unless --lower-better is given, and non-player columns are dropped (--drop-cols date)
win frequency is what matters; margins are ignored, so a small-wins big-losses player can top it
periods are comparable games and block bootstrap blocks capture their dependence

input.shape: a wide CSV with rows = periods and one numeric column per player (returns or losses), or a winner,loser[,draw] games CSV

name: chess-ladder
not_for: choosing the strategy that makes the most money (read it beside model-confidence-set or mean returns)
output: Elo-unit ratings with 90% bootstrap intervals, P(beats #1), and the list of players not separated from the leader

assumes: the reasons are in this text and use explicit causal markers
each reason restates the link with overlapping content words, else the chain stops UNSUPPORTED

input.shape: a text with a central causal claim and its own because / since / due to clauses

name: child-why-chain
not_for: an argument whose reasons are implicit or live in another document
output: a why-chain up to 5 deep with its stop reason: CIRCULAR, UNSUPPORTED or five whys reached

assumes: each part's provides, requires and invariants are declared by hand and complete; an undeclared assumption cannot clash
invariants with the same key mean the same thing across parts (mode: paper vs live)

input.shape: a Python list of 3+ part dicts {name, provides:set, requires:set, invariants:{key:value}}

name: chimera
not_for: finding a good combination - that is cross-breed; chimera only reports where a fusion breaks
output: {viable, conflicts (same invariant, different values), unmet_requires, provides, invariants}

assumes: the citation graph is written out by hand or by a script first; the tool does not extract cites from prose
a primary is an existing file under --base or a node marked primary; an existing file is trusted as evidence without reading its content
URLs count as primary only with --urls-primary

input.shape: one line per claim 'id <- cite, cite' (or JSONL with cites), citing receipts by path relative to --base

name: citogenesis-check
not_for: a prose report whose citations are not yet written as a claim graph, or checking whether the primary file actually supports the claim
output: per claim GROUNDED / SINGLE-SOURCE / UNGROUNDED / CIRCULAR with hop count, primaries and dangling cites; exit 1 on any CIRCULAR or UNGROUNDED

assumes: rows carry the access and status fields (or columns mappable to them); prose write-ups are not parsed
receipt paths resolve under --base (default the file's folder) on this machine
OVERSTATED is word-based (confirms, proven), so a strong claim in mild words passes

input.shape: research output rows as JSONL or CSV with claim, access, status and receipt/source/proof columns (mappable with --map)

name: claim-status-labels
not_for: a prose report with no per-row fields (use source-labels or research-integrity)
output: per bad row: UNLABELED / BAD-LABEL / NO-RECEIPT / NOT-RUN / CITED-UNREAD / NO-SOURCE / NO-PROOF / OVERSTATED; k/n rows clean; exit 1 on any

assumes: solution words are spelled as identifiers or code tokens - plain-English names of the solution slip through ('caching' does not match cache)
with solution= given, its common words (get, run, data) are masked too
the requirement is prose a sentence splitter can separate

input.shape: a requirement or spec text, optionally with the current solution's source file

name: clean-slate
not_for: a design doc that is meant to name the implementation
output: contamination ratio, count of pure-need sentences, the requirement restated with [_] masks

assumes: byte identity is the right notion of 'same' for the files (a CRLF or whitespace-only change counts as different)
the probes exercise the edges where the copy could drift (empty, boundary, degenerate cases); weak probes prove little
the callables are deterministic on the probes

input.shape: a source and its copy: two files (byte check) or two callables plus a list of probe inputs (behaviour check)

name: clone-check
not_for: proving a cache equals its slow path when the cache can be stale or incomplete (use fast-path-proof)
output: True/False match plus content fingerprints (sha) of each file or of each callable's outputs over the probes

assumes: the closing book was captured at the close for every bet, ideally from a sharp book
bets are independent (same-game or correlated bets make the CI too narrow)
odds are decimal odds

input.shape: a bet log CSV with market, odds_taken (decimal) and either close_book (';'-joined) with pick or close_prob

name: closing-line-value
not_for: a win/loss results log with no closing prices
output: per bet CLV and EV at close; mean CLV with 95% bootstrap CI and verdict beats / loses to / indistinguishable from the close; share beating the close with binomial p; per-market table

assumes: the task is non-trivial (one-line fixes, renames, config edits get 'no cage: trivial')
the change is uncommitted or on top of a known base ref so git diff shows exactly the caged work
a legal excellent DOOR exists under at most three bars; otherwise the cage is a wall and a bar must be swapped

input.shape: a coding task in a git repo or scratch clone; the receipt script reads git diff against a base ref

name: code-cage
not_for: reviewing someone else's finished code - the cage must be set before writing
output: a CAGE card (PLAIN, BURNED, BARS, DOOR, SPARK), the built code, and a RECEIPT: script summary (net lines, new imports, nesting, swallowed excepts...) plus KEPT/BENT/BROKEN per bar and a RENT verdict

assumes: name lenses trust prefixes (is_/get_/load_) and the ghost lens knows only this workspace's E/D/GT id formats with an errata/DECISIONS file nearby
race sees one function at a time and twins matches only <verb>_<rest> names
every finding is a lead read at its file:line and ruled REAL or FALSE ALARM by a person; nothing is a verdict

input.shape: one or more Python source folders (a project package); git history for the fossil lens

name: code-kaleidoscope
not_for: non-Python code, or a demand for a pass/fail verdict on code quality
output: findings per lens (liar, ghost, clamp, race, clock, echo, twins, hollow, shadow, mutable, floateq, fossil) with file:line, up to 15 per lens; --json for all

assumes: transcripts are Claude Code jsonl with Bash/PowerShell tool_use and tool_result paired by id
dialect is inferable from syntax markers; quoted text handed to another shell is stripped
fewer than 20 mismatches makes relative risk unreliable (TOO FEW)

input.shape: a Claude Code projects folder of .jsonl session transcripts (with subagents via --sub)

name: code-switch-audit
not_for: finding Windows-specific traps inside source code (windows-port-audit)
output: counts of shell calls matched / MISMATCHED / neutral, error rates and relative risk, per-marker counts, examples; --json

assumes: both series are aligned on the same timestamps with no gaps
the tie is stable over the sample - this is an in-sample test and regime changes break it
if many pairs were screened, about 5% pass by chance - deflate for the search

input.shape: two aligned price series of equal length

name: cointegration
not_for: two return series (already stationary), or a pair picked from a big screen with no deflation or holdout
output: {hedge_ratio, intercept, r2, adf_t, crit_5pct, cointegrated, half_life}

assumes: the recipe's command runs from its declared inputs alone in a scrubbed environment (PATH, SYSTEMROOT, TEMP only)
the replicator is not the builder session (self-replication is INVALID)
the inputs are unchanged between seal and verify, and the brief leaks no claimed value

input.shape: a recipe.json (command + declared input files) and a claims.json (name -> value or {value, tol}) for a result in a repo

name: cold-replication
not_for: a rerun inside the session that produced the number, or a result whose command needs network or undeclared files
output: a sealed packet (BRIEF.md, recipe.json with hashes) and, on verify, MATCH / MISMATCH / MISSING per claim with VERDICT REPLICATED / PARTIAL / FAILED / INVALID; exit 0/1/2

assumes: entries are short one-liners: long SKILL.md descriptions score low (closest live pair 0.20), so the 0.4 default finds nothing
duplicates share vocabulary (the same idea in other words does not collide)
the registry stays under a few thousand entries (exact all-pairs Jaccard)

input.shape: a name plus a one-line description of a new idea or skill, registered into an append-only JSONL registry

name: collision-registry
not_for: judging whether two ideas mean the same thing (it measures shared words, not meaning)
output: new / collision (ids, names, scores) / exists, appended to the JSONL registry; list shows entries and skipped corrupt lines

assumes: the tool can be run read-only against real data (no tour row may write the shared cache or send an order)
its flags are discoverable from --help and recent git log
command strings use POSIX paths (backslashes die in shlex)

input.shape: a command-line tool with --help, real data to run it on, and a tour file of (name, command) rows

name: command-tour
not_for: a library with no CLI, or a unit-test gap hunt - it finds usability friction, not code coverage
output: per row exit code, seconds, line count, head/tail and a full log; a friction list where each friction becomes one red-first test and one fix

assumes: snapshots cover the period that hurt, taken every few minutes; a crunch between snapshots is invisible
owners are attributed correctly by process-owner-map (a misattributed process blames the wrong owner)
the floor of free MB is chosen by the user (500 suggested); blame depends on it

input.shape: several timed memory snapshots (process-owner-map --json files) or a JSONL of {t, free_mb, owners}

name: commons-grazing
not_for: deciding whether to start a job now (memory-gate) or one snapshot with no crunch in it
output: crunch lines with deficit, fair share and blame per owner, then GRAZER / OVERSUBSCRIBED verdicts; exit 0 no crunch, 1 crunch, 2 bad args

assumes: moats are NAMED in words (proprietary data, history, scars); tacit skill is invisible
a moat word used loosely (our screener) is over-credited
items are separable as bullets or steps

input.shape: a venture page, strategy write-up or roadmap with step or bullet items

name: competitor-eye
not_for: measuring real competitive threat in a market (it judges the description only)
output: copyable list, moat list, thinnest moat with its net score; one summary line

assumes: only edges promoted through the forward pipeline carry status CONFIRMED
ret is the period's forward paper return from forward-score, not a backtest number
the policy numbers (reinvest, floor, cap, halt-dd) are judgement calls recorded in a decision row

input.shape: ledger.csv of date,edge,status,ret rows - forward paper returns per edge

name: compound-interest-edges
not_for: sizing positions - it allocates research budget only, paper-only
output: per date edges, equity, drawdown, budget and RUN / HALT, then 'next budget N (k unconfirmed rows not counted)'

assumes: cards use the '**C<n> · title**' notation (otherwise pass --card-re) and the default field set (otherwise --fields)
assumptions carry a closed tag HOLDS / FAILS / UNKNOWN, not 'partly'
forced code exists at --root when the forces check is wanted

input.shape: a plan markdown holding typed concept cards as '**C<n> · title**' lines with definition, theory, assumptions A1..An, forces and other fields

name: concept-card
not_for: a plan with no concept cards (it reports no card) or a glossary section that is meant to be definitions only
output: one row per problem (card id, line, NO_TAG / NO_TEST / GLOSSARY / missing field or missing forced function) and counts; exit 0 clean, 1 problems or no card, 2 bad args

assumes: each criticism is already split into its own point with an id
verdicts carry evidence; it checks the reply's structure, not whether a rejection is right

input.shape: criticisms split into ids, a verdict map (accept / reject / partial with evidence and fix), the retractions and the draft reply

name: concession-audit
not_for: deciding whether a criticism is actually right (it only checks one-verdict-per-point structure)
output: {ok, issues, counts}: points with no verdict, no evidence, accepted points with no fix, blanket-concession text, retractions outside what was criticised

assumes: evidence is detected by FORM (a number, path, link, test name) not checked - a made-up number counts as support
each sentence has at most one explanation marker that matters (only the first is read)
supporting evidence sits in the same or next sentence

input.shape: a prose explanation (postmortem, report, reply) with because/so/therefore sentences

name: confabulation-check
not_for: checking that cited numbers are true - follow with numbers-pass
output: each because/so explanation graded SUPPORTED or UNSUPPORTED with effect <- marker <- offered cause

assumes: certainty is read from a fixed hedge/booster lexicon; sarcasm, negated boosters and domain words that look like hedges are misread
sentences split cleanly (tables and code blocks distort the strip)
it measures how sure the text sounds, not whether the confidence is earned

input.shape: a note, report or reply in English prose, several sentences long

name: confidence-contour
not_for: judging whether a confident claim is true or calibrated (calibration-check, evidence-only)
output: a per-sentence strip of five levels (_ . - = #), mean level, peak, the biggest jumps, and certain sentences that carry no number

assumes: the files to check are STAGED (--staged reads index blobs, not the work tree)
fixtures holding markers on purpose are listed with --allow
the commit is chained on the gate's exit code, not with ;

input.shape: a repo with staged files after a conflict resolve (or work-tree files named directly)

name: conflict-marker-gate
not_for: semantic merge errors that leave no marker text (wrong side kept, duplicated rows)
output: MARKER file:line lines and VERDICT: BLOCK (exit 1) or VERDICT: CLEAN (exit 0); optional pre-commit hook

assumes: the quantities that must be conserved are declared up front
both before and after states are in memory
the tolerance suits the quantity (float totals need one)

input.shape: a before state, an after state and named functions state -> number for each conserved quantity

name: conserve-check
not_for: proving full equivalence of a refactor - only the quantities you named are checked
output: {all_conserved, violated, quantities{before, after, delta, conserved}}

assumes: keys are stable strings (sha256 of the key text decides placement)
enough virtual nodes for an even load (more vnodes, flatter load)
the workload tolerates ~1/n of keys moving when a node is added or removed

input.shape: node names and string keys passed in code to a Ring object

name: consistent-hash
not_for: a one-time balanced split into two (fission is simpler) or a partition that must never move any key
output: a Ring with node_for(key), add, remove and assignment(keys); moved keys always go to the new node

assumes: both captures used the same --files list and package mode
the difference that matters is in Python, platform, packages or tracked files (BLAS/MKL, CPU flags and OS patches are not captured)
installed package metadata matches what the code actually imported

input.shape: a Python environment on one machine (captured to JSON), or two env JSON captures to diff, optionally with files/folders to hash

name: container-image-instances
not_for: proving a data or code copy is faithful (use clone-check)
output: capture: JSON fingerprint (env var names only); diff: CRITICAL and other difference lines and VERDICT IDENTICAL / COMPATIBLE / DRIFTED, exit 0 / 1 / 2

assumes: the store root is used only through the tool (stray files are reported by verify)
hashes are 64 lowercase hex and ref names match [A-Za-z0-9._-]
one blob per ref is enough: there are no tree/manifest objects for multi-file snapshots

input.shape: bytes or files to store in a store root folder; Python API or the cas.py CLI (put/get/verify/ref/refs/gc)

name: content-store
not_for: versioned editing of a working file - it pins exact bytes, it does not diff or merge
output: a sha256 per put, re-hashed reads (IntegrityError on rot), verify-all (n, bad list), atomic named refs, gc of unreachable blobs

assumes: the answer opens with the Controlled Fire header naming controlled objects and one gate, and grades claims S0-S3
every number is traceable to the evidence text passed in; numbers from runs not passed as evidence are flagged untraced
whether a counter-example is the strongest or a theorem applies stays a human judgement the checker cannot see

input.shape: a derivation, proof, report or answer written in Controlled Fire form, plus the run output that its numbers trace to

name: controlled-fire
not_for: a casual answer or code change with no derivation or numerical claim
output: lint lines for header, grades and residual sentences, soft-gap language, counter-example order, ending, untraced numbers; termination FIXED POINT REACHED / NOT REACHED; a next-gate prompt

assumes: duplicates sit in DIFFERENT skill folders (same-skill twins are ignored on purpose)
functions have at least 4 statements; tiny helpers are skipped
near twins calling differently named helpers only match fuzzily, not exactly

input.shape: a root folder of skill folders, each holding Python tool files

name: convergence-detector
not_for: deciding a duplicate must be merged (a 5-line seeded RNG copy may be cheaper to keep than an import edge)
output: cross-skill function pairs above --threshold with Jaccard sim and exact flag, grouped into shared-module families ranked by skills x statements

assumes: points are two-dimensional
interior and collinear points are meant to be dropped
a convex outline is the right shape - a concave region is overstated

input.shape: a list of 2-D (x, y) points

name: convex-hull
not_for: higher-dimensional data or a frontier that must keep only the upper or concave side
output: CCW list of extreme points; point_in_hull True / False

assumes: timestamps match exactly between the feeds (resample first if not)
the feeds glitch independently; when both glitch at one timestamp the less-wrong print is kept
a bad print has neighbours for the local-median blame (first and last bars are weak)

input.shape: two ts,value CSVs of the same quantity from two independent feeds (or --ts-col / --val-col names)

name: convolve-signals
not_for: two feeds that disagree structurally (many suppressed prints; go back to second-source) or two different quantities
output: aligned count, unmatched timestamps, constant bias a-b, each SUPPRESSED print with the value the other feed implies; --series prints the consensus as ts,value

assumes: the inputs are returns aligned by date, equal length, >= 30 rows, no NaN/inf (else rejected)
enough tail days: below 20 per tail it warns (q=1% needs about 2000 rows)
one regime: in-sample tail dependence moves with regime

input.shape: two aligned return series of equal length >= 30 (a CSV with two named columns), no NaN or inf

name: copula-dependence
not_for: price levels or a whole portfolio (returns only, two series at a time)
output: Pearson, Spearman, Kendall tau, Gaussian rho from tau, per-q lower/upper tail dependence vs a simulated Gaussian copula, crash vs calm correlation vs Gaussian baselines

assumes: audits and probes run on a COPY of the library, never the live one
trigger phrases come from descriptions or real asks, never from body pitches (that games route-audit)
multi-word phrases do not collapse to one generic word after stopwords

input.shape: a skill library folder (a COPY for audit/probe) plus core_triggers.json and probe TSVs of real asks

name: core-skill-pin
not_for: routing a single ask - that is skill-finder; this tunes the router's pins
output: check: missing core skills and COLLAPSED phrases; audit: core/library top-1/top-5 before and after and skills that lost top-5; probe: hit@5 with FIXED/BROKE rows; table: markdown trigger table

assumes: costs and benefits are word counts, not magnitudes, unless items mode with numbers is used
every party named in a sentence receives that sentence's whole cost or benefit
parties are capitalised nouns or pronouns; metric names (Sharpe) can show up as false parties

input.shape: a plan, rule or proposal in prose naming parties (we, Max, users, sessions); or items JSON with real cost numbers

name: cost-to-whom
not_for: a quantified budget or P&L where magnitudes matter, or a text that names no parties
output: a table of cost and benefit counts per party, the biggest net payer and the biggest net gainer

assumes: a vote is a whole-word mention by a lens, not a judgement that the element matters
the seated lenses change as the lens family grows; pass lenses= to repeat a comparison
the subject is not a pure series (refused: no named elements)

input.shape: a note, plan, code file or item list (not a numeric series)

name: council-of-views
not_for: a price or return series, or a request for a reasoned judgement of importance
output: elements binned agreed / contested / lone dissent (dissenter named) / ignored with tallies and the council list

assumes: counts are insert-only (negative updates are rejected)
the items you care about are frequent - error is epsilon times the whole stream total N
sketches to merge share epsilon, delta and seed

input.shape: a stream of hashable items (symbols, event names) too large to count exactly

name: count-min-sketch
not_for: rare items, or a stream small enough to count exactly in a dict
output: per-item estimates that never undercount, heavy hitters above a threshold from a candidate list

assumes: causation is stated with connectors (because, due to, so, therefore, led to, if-then); implicit causation is missed
rival causes and witnesses share content words with the effect
it only frames the question; nothing is tested

input.shape: a postmortem, verdict or because-story in prose with explicit causal connectors

name: counterfactual-view
not_for: establishing that a cause really mattered (it runs nothing), or text where causation is implied ('the outage cost us a day')
output: one 'if NOT (cause) - would (effect) still happen?' pair per causal claim (one per part of a compound cause), plus rival causes and witness sentences the text names

assumes: the strategy name holds a known style word (carry, reversion, momentum...) for the archetype match
one flat spread_bps fits every item

input.shape: strategy items with name, sharpe, turnover, drawdown (JSON or CSV), or a text of trade and market claims

name: counterparty-view
not_for: finding who actually traded against you (textbook archetypes, not market data)
output: per item the counterparty archetype, why they trade, the spread turnover pays market makers and a flag where return per drawdown is below median; text mode flips each claim into the counterparty's bet

assumes: observations are roughly iid in time (the 1/n ML sample covariance of the paper)
the scaled-identity target is reasonable; with a strong common market factor shrinkage helps on average but not in every sample

input.shape: rows = observations over time, columns = assets (returns), called from Python

name: cov-shrinkage
not_for: a price-level table - feed returns, not prices
output: the shrunk covariance matrix and the intensity delta (near 1 = data too thin), plus an is_positive_definite check

assumes: the rule uses only comparisons, and/or/not, arithmetic, numbers, variables and function calls; no crosses_above-style temporal operators and no strings
functions are opaque, so rules that differ only inside a function's meaning look equal
EQUIVALENT means no difference in N random trials, not a proof; > vs >= ties on continuous draws are not seen

input.shape: one or two rule expressions as strings, infix screener style (close > sma(close, 50) and rsi(14) < 30) or s-expressions

name: creole-from-two-tongues
not_for: a Pine script or a rule file with temporal operators, or proving two rules equal on edge values (tolerance-edge)
output: the translated rule (to-sexpr / to-infix / ast), or EQUIVALENT (exit 0) / DIFFERENT with a counterexample environment (exit 1)

assumes: errata quote the bad code in a code span in the BUG half (before now/fixed/instead); errata with no span grow nothing
grown spacers are read by a person and fix-side rows deleted
only added lines of a unified diff with +++ b/ headers are scanned

input.shape: errata.md files (to grow spacers) and a unified diff or git diff --cached (to scan added lines)

name: crispr-errata-immunity
not_for: a bug class that was never written into an erratum with quoted code
output: grow: new spacer rows in spacers.jsonl; scan: file:line repeats errata:Eid lines and a hit count; exit 1 on any hit

assumes: times are UTC or naive wall clock - time zones and DST are out of scope
the target scheduler uses Vixie semantics (restricted DOM OR restricted DOW)
no @reboot and no 6-field seconds syntax

input.shape: one 5-field cron expression or @daily-style macro

name: cron-parse
not_for: Windows Task Scheduler triggers or a local-time schedule across a DST change
output: plain-English explanation, lint warnings, next N runs, previous run, fires_at; CronError on bad fields

assumes: a metric exists to judge hybrid vigor: the child must beat BOTH parents on it
the parents are genuinely different (self-pairs and duplicates are culled)
soup output is candidates only; each needs vigor proof and a failing-capable selftest before it becomes a skill

input.shape: two or more parents (skill names, words, numbers, signals, modules) and a mode, BROAD or 1-TO-1

name: cross-breed
not_for: merging two files or branches (a union or merge job), or treating soup candidates as built skills
output: fitting reproduction operators with their sibling skills; a vigor verdict KEEP / STERILE / DEPRESSION; skill_soup gives a list of named candidate children {name, parents, operator, blurb}

assumes: a row may only cite ids defined above it; any forward citation is flagged
ids follow one pattern the default or --def / --ref regexes can match

input.shape: a numbered, ordered record whose rows define ids and cite them (DECISIONS.md tables, errata headings, numbered plans)

name: cross-cutting-check
not_for: documents that cite later items on purpose (a plan whose cards reference later cards)
output: INTRUSION / PHANTOM / INVERSION / DUPLICATE_DEF findings with line numbers, or a --summary count; exit 0 conformable, 1 findings, 2 bad args

assumes: master and segment are the same asset and bar size (otherwise UNDATED)
the segment is long enough and non-periodic, or the margin test reports AMBIGUOUS
the master covers the plausible window (runtime is O(null x master x segment))
