input.shape: a dated master CSV (time, value columns) and an undated segment of the same quantity at the same bar size

name: cross-date
not_for: aligning two dated feeds that disagree on values - use second-source
output: DATED with start/end timestamps, r, runner-up margin and shuffle p; or AMBIGUOUS / UNDATED; exit 0/1/2

assumes: both streams share one clock and units; time zones and exchange vs receive time are converted first
events are sparse relative to tol so greedy one-to-one matches the global optimum; dense events make it ambiguous
the match fraction is read against chance_frac; on a perfectly periodic stream chance is overstated

input.shape: two time-stamped event streams (two CSVs whose first column is a time in the same units, or two float lists)

name: crossmatch
not_for: aligning two bar series value by value (indicator-parity) or a single stream
output: one-to-one pairs with lag, unmatched events on each side, lag median/MAD/5-95%, ambiguous and duplicate counts, match fraction vs chance fraction

assumes: all forecasts are of the same quantity in the same unit
3 or more forecasts
the diversity theorem is about squared error of the mean; it says nothing about calibration

input.shape: 3 or more forecasts of the same number (values list or items with a numeric column), optionally a truth value

name: crowd-view
not_for: probabilistic forecasts of binary events whose calibration is the question (calibration-check)
output: crowd mean, median, diversity; with truth: crowd error vs mean individual error, who beat the crowd, crowd rank

assumes: the neighbour relation is supplied and finite
compatibility is local and pairwise - growth is transitive, so a gradual drift can chain far from the seed
you choose the seed

input.shape: seed items plus a neighbors_of(item) function and a compatible(a, b) test

name: crystallize
not_for: partitioning a whole set into clusters (gravity-cluster, k-means)
output: the grown region (set of items reachable through compatible neighbours)

assumes: auto mode reads levels vs increments correctly; positive counts can be misread (force --opt mode=increments)
the series is at most a few thousand points (O(n^2) window search)
the net total is non-trivial, so a share of it is meaningful

input.shape: a P&L or increment series (or levels, auto-differenced) of up to a few thousand points

name: cumulative-view
not_for: drawdown depth and duration statistics (use drawdown-stats)
output: net total, the shortest window holding the chosen share of it, the half-way step, the running peak and giveback after it, and the longest flat stretch

assumes: outcomes are written in plain outcome words (time, money, risk, effort); an outcome in technical words reads as a feature
a feature's so-what shares a content word with an outcome sentence

input.shape: a pitch, venture page or release note in sentences

name: customer-eye
not_for: judging whether there is real demand (use demand-scan)
output: FEATURE / OUTCOME / CONTEXT per sentence, the features-to-outcomes ratio, and features with no so-what anywhere

assumes: the real system can be cast as agents that each push a shared quantity one way and grow best near a preferred value
parameters are valid (albedos in [0,1] in order; q below S*L/sigma) or Params.validate refuses them
the generic rein-control version is cited from memory and needs verification

input.shape: model parameters (Params) or a list of (effect, preference) agent types for the generic rein-control sweep

name: daisyworld
not_for: fitting real data - it is a parable model; it does not estimate anything from a series
output: sweep tables (T_up, T_down, T_dead, covers) and the regulated range width with life vs the lifeless baseline, with hysteresis visible

assumes: each function can be called with the single --arg value and has no side effects worth worrying about when called thousands of times
the call costs more than three times the empty call's jitter, else it is BELOW NOISE FLOOR and --number must rise
machine load is roughly steady across the interleaved rounds

input.shape: two or more importable functions as file.py:func with one argument value to call them on

name: dark-frame
not_for: proving a faster version gives the same answers (speed-proof) or timing a whole script or pipeline
output: dark-frame time and noise, per function raw time, signal above dark, SNR, raw and dark-corrected ratio and FASTER / NO DIFFERENCE / BELOW NOISE FLOOR; exit 0 difference, 1 none, 2 bad input

assumes: T comfortably larger than N and no missing values (fill or trim first)
each asset's residuals are serially exchangeable; overlapping or autocorrelated residuals make the null too easy
residuals come from an already fitted model; raw returns just find the market factor

input.shape: CSV residual panel: one row per asset (first column name), equal-length residual series, T well above N, up to ~80 assets

name: dark-matter
not_for: naming what the missing factor is (correlate the series with candidates afterwards)
output: MISSING FACTOR(S) / NO COMMON FACTOR with n_significant and per factor eigenvalue, var share, MP edge, perm95, loadings, series

assumes: the file has a date column and OHLC(V) columns at a declared bar size
items 5, 6, 8, 10 (adjustments, survivorship, revision, terms) need a person - they come back as ask
an as-of date is given so the forming bar and staleness can be judged

input.shape: one symbol's OHLCV bar file (CSV) from a new source, or two snapshots of it for revision depth

name: data-hygiene
not_for: tick or trade-tape data, or a non-price table
output: refuse / warn / ask lists (granularity, duplicate and missing days, forming bar, 5x breaks, bad OHLC, device names, sha256, staleness); revision_window.py: deepest revised bar in hours

assumes: the batch fits in memory (thousands of rows, not gigabytes)
row order is stable: the same rows reordered hash as a new batch, so duplicate detection misses them
the WAL has not been compacted (duplicates are found from WAL records), and cross-batch continuity is checked elsewhere

input.shape: one batch of feed rows (CSV) plus a contract.json, a content-store folder and a WAL path

name: data-intake
not_for: gigabyte files or checking continuity between batches (gaps, overlaps across drops)
output: status clean / quarantined / rejected / duplicate, the batch sha256 (its store key), the stored raw (and clean/bad subsets when quarantined) and one WAL record

assumes: versions are integers that only rise
payloads compare as exact sorted JSON (0.1 vs 0.10000000001 is a CONFLICT)
the first file is the primary and a timestamp column exists for lag seconds

input.shape: a primary JSONL truth store plus one or more replica copies; rows carry a key, an integer version and a timestamp

name: db-replication-ledger
not_for: an append-only log without per-key versions (use uncommitted-record-sentinel or backup-witness)
output: per key SAME / LAGGING / CONFLICT / AHEAD / MISSING / ORPHAN / SELF-CONFLICT; per replica FRESH / STALE / DIVERGED; exit 0 / 1 / 2

assumes: verdict lines carry dates the parser reads ('10-07' style takes --year) and DEAD/OPEN/ALIVE/CORRECTED words
every lane word appears in the verdict line (5-letter stem match); a line naming two lanes can mislead
the record is complete: exit 1 (no verdict) does not prove the lane is new

input.shape: verdict record folders/files (memory notes, GRAVEYARD.md, receipts) searched for a 1-3 word lane name

name: dead-lane-check
not_for: deciding whether a DEAD verdict is stale - that is lane-resurrection
output: lane '<words>': STANDING DEAD/OPEN/ALIVE (date) <- file:line plus earlier lines; exit 3 DEAD, 0 open/alive, 1 none found

assumes: the registration states a per-step expected return and volatility in the same units as the record; with no registered mu there is nothing to walk against
steps are roughly independent with constant sigma (the cone is sigma*sqrt(k))
an exit is read against the model-exit percentage, since the registered model itself leaves the band often (about 22% in 20 steps)

input.shape: a forward record of per-step returns in time order (text or JSONL with --field) plus the registered per-step mu and sigma

name: dead-reckoning-cone
not_for: a backtest with no pre-registered mu and sigma, or deciding when to stop a forward test (sprt-sequential)
output: ON-COURSE (exit 0) / BELOW-COURSE / ABOVE-COURSE (exit 1), INDISTINGUISHABLE-FROM-ZERO flag, last and max z, the step it left the cone, and the model-exit probability

assumes: origin/main was fetched just before (the tools never fetch)
rows are markdown table rows | Dnnn | ...; range key rows are notes and ignored
two sessions may take the next free number at the same minute; claim it on #41 first

input.shape: a repo's DECISIONS.md (or errata / GT ids) on main versus a branch or merged tree that drafted its own numbers

name: decision-renumber
not_for: editing or rewording an existing row on main (only Max can order that)
output: check_decisions: APPEND_ONLY, DUPLICATE, ROW_EDITED_OR_REMOVED, OUT_OF_ORDER, GAPS, NEXT_FREE, VERDICT; next_free_id: next id and CLASH list (exit 1)

assumes: a declaration exists (header in the first 50 lines or --expect) and is itself correct
the counter mode matches the record format (--regex / --jsonl / --csv / --table / --lines)
a matching count is enough - it does not prove the right records were read

input.shape: a data file (JSONL, CSV, pipe table, regex lines) with EXPECTED_<NAME>: n in its first 50 lines, or a count given

name: declared-count
not_for: checking record content or types (schema-contract)
output: pass, or DeclaredCountError 'declared N, counted M (+/-d) - halting'

assumes: the module can be wrapped as a one-step forecast; its value is judged by one-step MSE (a sizing or timing module needs a PnL world)
the planted worlds chosen (ar1, season, regime, or a custom one) match what the module claims to find
the null world is kept so a look-ahead shows as SUSPECT-LEAK

input.shape: a python module exposing forecast(history) -> next value, named as module.py:func

name: decorative-check
not_for: a module whose job is sizing, timing or filtering trades without a forecast wrapper
output: per world mean dMSE, t, p and beats-flat; VERDICT EARNS-ITS-KEEP (exit 0) / DECORATIVE (exit 3) / SUSPECT-LEAK (exit 4)

assumes: regimes differ in the mean or volatility of steps (correlation or autocorrelation regimes are invisible)
the series is long enough to split (minimum regime max(5, n/20) bars)

input.shape: a price or value series (CSV) whose most recent bars form the window being judged

name: deep-time
not_for: a short series (one regime on 24 bars means too little data, not stability)
output: the window's share of history, regimes before it, regimes it spans, and window vs full volatility ratio

assumes: the prompt archive files exist and hold the prompts of interest (unarchived prompts cannot be reached)
prompts are long enough that Jaccard links are not just common words ('keep', 'going'); short prompts give shallow wanders
the archive uses '### ' headings to separate prompts

input.shape: a short subject phrase or text, walked against an archive of Max's prompts split at '### ' headings (default C:/Autotrade/MAX_PROMPTS_*.md)

name: default-mode-wander
not_for: finding prompts ABOUT a topic - that is prompt-genealogy; this deliberately surfaces the least related ones
output: WANDERED to idea <id> (visits, similarity, hops via bridge word): the old prompt text, with the bridge path

assumes: trial_sharpes includes every configuration evaluated, the discarded ones too; leaving failures out understates N
Sharpes are per-period, not annualized, matching the return series length
the returns carry no look-ahead and the dataset is unbiased; DSR corrects selection and non-normality only

input.shape: the best strategy's per-period returns plus the per-period Sharpes of EVERY configuration tried

name: deflated-sharpe
not_for: a single pre-registered strategy with no search, or a result whose trial count is unknown
output: sharpe, sr0 (expected max of N skill-less trials), PSR vs zero, DSR and n_trials; break_even_trials gives the number of trials before DSR falls below target

assumes: names are found by capitalization; a capitalized sentence-opener is kept and mid-sentence capitalized common words get blurred
argues is a keyword test, not a logic check

input.shape: a pitch, argument or report in prose with numbers, names and sources

name: defocus
not_for: deciding whether the remaining argument is valid (run doubt-mind or smuggled-premise on the skeleton)
output: sentence skeleton with <NUM> <PCT> <NAME> <SOURCE> tokens, each tagged argues / details only, and a specificity share

assumes: demand is measured against the TF-IDF router, not real use - a skill invoked by name can show zero
the --weak bar is absolute and drifts with library size
prompts of under 4 routable words are not asks and are skipped

input.shape: the skill library plus Max's real prompts read from session transcripts

name: demand-scan
not_for: deleting a skill on its own say-so - zero demand is a candidate list only
output: per skill hits and top1 counts, zero-demand list (retire candidates), unserved asks (gaps)

assumes: periods are of equal length
the series has no strong trend: labels are relative to the whole-series mean and sd, so a trend makes early periods all lean
lean means lean for this series only; there is no absolute cutoff

input.shape: a list of per-period magnitudes (commits per week, revenue per month) passed to read_rings in code

name: dendro
not_for: a trending series (run erosion first) or telling a lasting regime change from a rough patch (changepoint)
output: fat / normal / lean label per period, fattest and leanest, longest drought and its start, good years, mean

assumes: the plan has 'Depth in the nooks of X' blocks whose X matches an existing section heading
a depth bullet names its item by number or shares a 4+ letter title word with it

input.shape: a markdown plan with numbered sections and 'Depth in the nooks of section X' blocks

name: depth-in-the-nooks
not_for: a plan with no depth blocks (it reports nothing, which is not completeness)
output: per block items / depth lines / problems; NO_DEPTH, NO_CONCEPT, THEORY_NO_STATUS, NO_SECTION findings; exit 0 / 1 / 2

assumes: the ask is supplied, or the text opens with its question
relevance shows as shared 5-letter stems; synonym-only answers fall to foreground and off-topic sentences repeating the ask's words land in focus

input.shape: a reply or document plus the ask (given with --opt ask=..., or the text's first sentence)

name: depth-of-field
not_for: judging whether the answer is correct - it measures topical overlap only
output: every sentence sorted in-focus / foreground / background, and the share of words in focus

assumes: conclusions carry a verdict marker word; sentences without one are left alone
negation is a word-level rewrite and can produce awkward grammar
the counters are arguments to test, not findings; a counter can be weaker than the claim

input.shape: a note, plan or report whose sentences state conclusions (verdict markers: so, therefore, will, should, always)

name: devils-advocate
not_for: a data table or code; or a request for evidence that refutes the claim (falsifier-view)
output: per conclusion its class (causal, numeric, absolute, forecast, recommendation), an exposure score and a templated counter-argument, most exposed first

assumes: only ONE knob varies; interactions need epistasis-scan
at least about 8 settings, or PEAK vs JAGGED is a rough call
the heuristic thresholds (5% steps, 10% extremes) suit the curve's scale

input.shape: a one-knob parameter sweep: y per setting as a series or rows with x and y columns, ideally 8+ settings

name: dial-sweep
not_for: deciding the best setting is real rather than selected from noise (noise-pick-force)
output: shape class RISING / FALLING / PEAK / VALLEY / PLATEAU / FLAT / JAGGED, best x, edge flag, near-best plateau width

assumes: the series is a growth curve, not a noisy random walk
flat_tol relative to the span separates a plateau from slow growth
noise is smaller than flat_tol, else steps flip between G and F at random

input.shape: a growth or adoption curve, mostly rising

name: diauxie
not_for: noisy price series - a G/F/G pattern there is noise (use changepoint)
output: {diauxic, pattern (G/F/D per step), lag_span}

assumes: diffpatch.py gets single-file patches only (multi-file diff --git streams go to patch_apply.py)
context lines are unchanged in the target; there is no fuzz, a changed context line is a rejection
conflicts are judged by line ranges only; non-overlapping edits can still be semantically incompatible

input.shape: two versions of one text file, or a unified patch plus its target file, or a saved multi-file git patch plus a repo (patch_apply.py)

name: diff-patch
not_for: a semantic merge of two edits that touch different lines but depend on each other
output: a unified diff; the patched text or REJECTED naming the hunk, line and differing text (exit 1); conflict pairs of base ranges; patch_apply reports each hunk APPLIED / ALREADY / FAILED / AMBIGUOUS

assumes: edge direction is meaningful: an edge confers importance on its target
the graph is passed as a Python dict (no file loader)

input.shape: a directed adjacency dict {node: [out-neighbors]} in memory, plus optional seed nodes

name: diffuse-rank
not_for: finding single points of failure whose removal fragments the graph (use keystone-find)
output: {node: score} summing to about 1 (personalized PageRank from the seeds)

assumes: errors are independent and normal; correlated separate errors must be merged into one shared input
every rung's own model error is declared (a missing own_sd makes the band too narrow)
the linear method holds locally; when nonlinear fires or an input is near a pole, the Monte Carlo is the answer

input.shape: Python: inputs {name: (value, sd)} and an ordered list of rungs (name, fn(env), own_sd, relative)

name: distance-ladder
not_for: a single product of ranged factors with no chain - fermi-estimate is simpler
output: final value, linear sd, MC sd and 5-95% band, variance share per source, per-rung amplification with AMPLIFIED/nonlinear flags

assumes: the scripts a doc names resolve relative to the doc's folder; repo-relative paths (tools/jobs.py) show as MISSING_SCRIPT outside the repo
a flag counts as known when it appears as a quoted literal, bare argv key or '--' + name build in the script or a local helper it imports
all-caps script names (X.py) are treated as placeholders and skipped

input.shape: a SKILL.md, README or plan file, or a folder (every SKILL.md below it; --all-md for every .md) that shows python X.py commands

name: doc-truth
not_for: docs whose commands are not python scripts (PowerShell, gh) or checking that the documented behaviour is right
output: MISSING_SCRIPT / UNKNOWN_FLAG / UNKNOWN_COMMAND lines with doc:line, a count per class; --run-selftest catches stale PASS counts; exit 0 clean, 1 problems, 2 bad args

assumes: periods align by bar offset, not calendar; the longer period is cut to the shorter
the KS distance has no p-value; autocorrelated steps make naive significance too optimistic
text mode compares word sets, so rewording reads as change

input.shape: one price series CSV split at a bar, or a text with two halves separated by ---

name: double-exposure
not_for: locating WHEN a change happened (changepoint) or claiming a significant regime change
output: KS step distance, widest rebased gap and its bar, per-period step mean and volatility; for text only_first / only_second words

assumes: the computation can be rerun or narrowed one variable at a time
the number has a real-world magnitude to test against
a red proof can be made that removes only the fix, not the feature

input.shape: a result just obtained: a number, two checks that disagree, a new test that passed, a peer's 'it is green'

name: doubt-mind
not_for: a formal significance or deflation test of an edge (signal-nulls, deflated-sharpe)
output: a named verdict TRUSTED / FRAGILE (with reasons) / UNDERPOWERED / NOT VERIFIED; helpers p_floor, magnitude_check, mean_check

assumes: callers live in the same file and call the target by bare name (imports, methods and other files are not seen)
for a plan, consumption is inferred from shared nouns and 'the result' anaphora (heuristic)
the target exists in the file (with no target it picks the widest downstream node)

input.shape: one python module (or a numbered plan) with an optional target function name or step number

name: downstream-view
not_for: a multi-module package where the real callers sit in other files (the blast radius is undercounted)
output: transitive consumers D1, D2... with how each call site uses the value (kept, dead, passed, returned, discarded) and the blast radius as a share of nodes

assumes: periods_per_year matches the data (252 daily stocks, 365 daily crypto, 52 weekly)
returns are already net of costs: Sharpe uses a zero risk-free rate and no cost model
one path is one sample: the numbers carry no interval (use bootstrap-ci)

input.shape: an equity curve, or per-period returns turned into one, as a Python list

name: drawdown-stats
not_for: a gross backtest return series judged without costs or intervals
output: {max_drawdown, peak/trough index, recovery periods (None if never), longest underwater, current drawdown, cagr, ann_vol, sharpe, sortino, calmar}, undefined ratios as None

assumes: sentences are short enough to cut at the first verb (subjects over 8 tokens or predicates over 16 are skipped, so run-on bullets drop out)
a bridge is shared words, not meaning, so a human must screen the kept dreams

input.shape: a research state note or session summary of many short declarative sentences

name: dream-logic
not_for: code, tables or bullet fragments with no verbs - nothing splits into subject and predicate
output: DREAM sentences (subject of #i + predicate of #j, bridged by #k...) - questions to test, never findings

assumes: there are at least two documents; one document cannot dream
terms are single words of 4+ letters, so code files contribute identifiers and noise
pairs are graded by co-occurrence, not meaning; a dream is a seed graded awake, never a finding

input.shape: a folder or list of many past documents (transcript digests, notes, findings files), at least two documents, capped by --max-mb

name: dream-recombination
not_for: recombining sentences inside one text (dream-logic) or crossing two chosen things (cross-breed)
output: seeded ranked term pairs from different documents, labelled BRIDGED (with bridge terms) or WILD, with their source documents; KNOWN pairs dropped

assumes: percent metrics need all values > 0 (otherwise skipped)
the default shift (half the absolute mean) and scale 2 are meaningful tilts for this data

input.shape: a numeric series (prices) or items JSON with an x and y column

name: dutch-angle
not_for: deciding which frame or unit is the correct one (a modelling choice it does not make)
output: each of 13 statistics classed moves with / invariant / DISTORTED with factor; for items elasticity, intercept, verdict

assumes: about 20+ points, so each decile edge holds more than one point
for a series the steps (changes), not the levels, are what you want split
a descriptive read is enough - no significance test

input.shape: a numeric series (its step changes are used) or items / table with numeric fields

name: edge-of-map
not_for: a significance claim about the tails (evt-tail, bootstrap-ci)
output: edge share of all movement, edge vs centre net move with DISAGREE flag, edge clustering in time; for items, who owns the edges

assumes: the strings are short (O(len a x len b))
character edits are the right notion of similarity (not meaning, word order or synonyms)
case and spacing are normalised beforehand if they should not count

input.shape: short strings (tickers, names, titles) and an optional candidate list, passed in code

name: edit-distance
not_for: whole documents, or look-alike records that differ in meaning (use candidate-then-gate)
output: edit distance (Levenshtein or OSA), the edit script that rebuilds the target, a 0-1 similarity, and the best match from a list with its distance

assumes: the design_state.md is read first and the question is not already settled there
ideas map onto a real Autotrade primitive (chain, certificate, gate, Tries Log, registry, pen); unmappable ones are LATER or OUT
every bullet carries an epistemic label (Established / Observed / Assumed / Inferred / Speculative / Unknown) and Observed items name their source

input.shape: a design question or Max's pasted idea list, run through one of 23 prompt files; its tool lints a markdown design-state section of labelled bullets

name: effort-relief
not_for: a quick code fix or a single factual question (it is a long design protocol)
output: a design pass written to design_state.md; label_check prints ERROR / WARN lines (unlabelled bullet, Observed without source, Assumed worded as a result)

assumes: the hatch condition is a single context key the caller can measure at check time (free_mb, a date, a flag)
the frozen spec text is self-contained; anything it references outside itself is not hashed and can drift

input.shape: Python: a spec text to freeze plus one hatch condition (context key, operator >= > <= < == exists, value)

name: egg-lay
not_for: scheduling a job to actually run - it only gates; something else must poll is_hatchable (see memory-gate)
output: an egg (spec, sha256 genome, hatch condition); is_hatchable returns True only when the condition holds and the spec is untampered

assumes: posts carry explicit CLAIM lines with a stance; free prose posts contribute nothing
the posts are exported first (gh issue view 41 --comments); the tool does not fetch from GitHub
sessions citing the same source are one voice only when the source field is filled; weights and the log-odds unit are judgement calls

input.shape: exported mailbox posts as JSONL {session, claim, stance, grade, source, ts} or a text dump of posts split by --- with FROM: lines and 'CLAIM key: SUPPORTS|REFUTES [grade]' lines

name: egregore-mailbox
not_for: a raw mailbox export with no CLAIM-tagged lines, or checking a claim against the world rather than against what sessions said
output: per claim a belief probability and BELIEVED / OPEN / CONTESTED with ECHO flags, support and refute weight, session and independent-voice counts

assumes: a PIN.json was written when the module was copied in (no pin, no baseline)
files are compared by sha256 (CRLF folded), not by lines; hunks need diff-patch
the upstream copy given is the version you want to compare against

input.shape: a vendored module folder, its PIN.json manifest, and optionally an upstream copy folder

name: endosymbiosis
not_for: a module that was never pinned, or comparing two arbitrary folders with no common ancestor
output: per file PRISTINE / LOCAL-EDIT / UPSTREAM-MOVED / CONFLICT / CONVERGED / LOCAL-ADDED / UPSTREAM-ADDED / LOCAL-MISSING; VERDICT exit 0 CLEAN, 1 DRIFTED, 2 CONFLICT

assumes: the invariants are known and expressible as pairwise relations
the fields are present in the state (a missing value counts as a break)
float relations carry their own tolerance

input.shape: a state dict plus declared bonds between field pairs (EQUAL, OPPOSITE, sum_to, ordered or a custom relation)

name: entanglement
not_for: proving a quantity is unchanged across a transformation (conserve-check)
output: {coherent, violations[{bond, a, b, a_val, b_val}]}

assumes: the buckets are a meaningful, exhaustive partition (an 'other' bucket or split labels change the reading)
the concentrated / heat-death thresholds suit the use (they are tunable)
distributions compared across different bucket counts use normalized entropy

input.shape: a list of bucket counts (category frequencies) passed to diagnose() in code

name: entropy-meter
not_for: continuous values that were never bucketed, or judging whether a distribution is correct rather than how spread it is
output: entropy in bits, normalized entropy 0..1, bucket count and a state label concentrated / structured / heat-death

assumes: the use is descriptive only: the centered trend uses future bars, so the envelope must never feed a signal
no single shock dominates (one crash widens the trailing range for a whole window)
the window matches the cycle of interest (default n/8, at least 4)

input.shape: a price or value series file (one column of closes)

name: envelope-view
not_for: building a trading signal or backtest feature (look-ahead by design)
output: envelope WIDENING / NARROWING / steady with late vs early amplitude ratio, slope per bar, and where it widened and narrowed fastest

assumes: the config is a flat-ish dict where an overlay key fully replaces the base value (no deep merge semantics promised)
callers read the effective() config rather than the base, or the marks have no effect

input.shape: Python: a base config dict and an overlay of marks {key: value}

name: epigenetic-switch
not_for: persisting a new default - when the base itself should change, edit the base and record why
output: effective config (base overlaid by marks, base untouched), new mark overlays, inherited child marks, and clear_marks reverting to the base

assumes: the chosen lenses can read this subject kind; lenses that cannot are skipped silently
a lens's verdict polarity is read from its structured stat, falling back to words; LOW-CONFIDENCE EPIPHANY lines are lexical guesses
the log file is written only when --opt log=PATH is given

input.shape: a series, text or plan the pov-core lenses can read, plus a lens list (or a seeded sample of n lenses); or a records.json of past runs

name: epiphany-log
not_for: a subject no pov-core lens reads (code, git history), or deciding which flipped verdict is right
output: the plain verdict, each lens's verdict, and EPIPHANY lines for every polarity flip; optional append to a JSONL log

assumes: every pair's level combinations are present with equal cell counts (else the pair is rejected)
runs are comparable (same period, same costs); only the toggles differ
only pairwise interactions matter; three-way terms are left in the residual

input.shape: CSV factorial grid: one row per run with toggle or parameter level columns and an outcome column, every level combination present

name: epistasis-scan
not_for: a one-knob sweep (dial-sweep) or a grid with missing level combinations
output: main effects, pairs ranked by p with BH survivors starred, ALIASED flags, signed 2x2 effects, an EPISTASIS line, discoveries list

assumes: the center is a surface word (plural -s folded); synonyms count as different topics
a sentence that mentions the center in passing is erased whole
enough sentences that keyword spans differ

input.shape: a note, text or plan of several sentences or steps

name: erase-the-center
not_for: finding the causal hero of a result (remove-the-hero)
output: center word, units remaining, new center, words that vanish with it

assumes: readings are roughly serially independent; an autocorrelated series (prices, cumulative totals) gives false significance
the change is a gradual monotone drift, not one jump (that is changepoint)
few ties; significance is |Z| > 1.96 only (no multiple-testing correction)

input.shape: an ordered list of metric readings passed to mann_kendall() in code

name: erosion
not_for: a price level series or any strongly autocorrelated series, or an abrupt level shift
output: trend increasing / decreasing / no trend with S, Kendall tau, Z, significant flag and n

assumes: the facts that matter are surface tokens (4+ letter words, tokens with digits) or are named with keys; a paraphrase that keeps a fact in other words reads as a loss
the hops form one ordered chain, each derived from the previous

input.shape: an original text and its chain of rewrites in order (hop1, hop2 ...), each a file; or sigma and L for the theory

name: error-threshold
not_for: comparing two independent rewrites of the same source (they are not a chain)
output: per-hop retention, geometric-mean fidelity Q, safe_hops before falling under the floor, the hop where keys were lost, and the Eigen key limit ln(sigma)/u

assumes: the command runs through this PC's Bash layer, where a doubled backslash arrives halved (measured 2026-10-13)
the risky text sits in a heredoc body or a python -c argument; other escape routes are not scanned
as a hook it is installed by Max's choice in settings.json and never blocks on its own error

input.shape: one Bash command string (a heredoc or python -c carrying Python, regexes or Windows paths), or a PreToolUse hook event on stdin

name: escape-proof
not_for: PowerShell commands - PowerShell does not treat backslash as an escape
output: 'ok' or the reason the command will be mangled plus the fix (use Write); as a hook, a block with that reason

assumes: inputs are continuous; discrete inputs (counts, categories) and flip regions narrower than the 15% scan step can be missed
the scales mean the noise you care about (one-bar moves vs data revisions vs cross-vendor differences)
joint search is exhaustive over pairs only up to 12 inputs

input.shape: a Python rule callable taking a dict of named numeric inputs, the current input values, and a scale (sd) per input or its history

name: escape-velocity
not_for: asking whether the rule is right or pays (forward-score); a large margin only says the call was stable
output: per input the smallest signed sd and raw move that flips the decision and its flip point; the joint minimum-norm flip; verdict FRAGILE / MARGINAL / SOLID / UNREACHABLE

assumes: simulated time only; real timers must drive run_until from a loop
single-threaded use
recurring float steps like 0.1 drift by rounding over very many repeats; cancelled entries stay in the heap until popped

input.shape: events scheduled through the Scheduler library API (time, payload or fn, priority, every, count)

name: event-scheduler
not_for: a real wall-clock cron or multi-threaded job queue (cron-parse, OS scheduler)
output: run_until returns [(time, payload)] fired in (time, priority, FIFO) order; now advances

assumes: event windows do not overlap much (overlap inflates the stacked response)
event indices were knowable at the time (no look-ahead)
dozens of events, not ten

input.shape: a return series plus the bar indices where a signal fired

name: event-stacking
not_for: a tradable-edge claim - no costs and no out-of-sample
output: {n_events, dropped_edge, overlapping, mean_path, car_path, car, ci95, placebo_p, snr}

assumes: activity is |change| of the series itself; volume or trade-count bars need cumulative volume as the input
the threshold (default 3x the mean absolute step) gives enough bars; with few bars the kurtosis comparison is noise
the clock bars are evenly spaced

input.shape: a CSV price or metric series in clock-time bars

name: event-time
not_for: building real volume or dollar bars from tick data without first passing cumulative volume
output: event bars (start, end, move), clock steps per event bar, fastest and slowest bars, activity split between halves, kurtosis in activity vs clock time

assumes: a marker is not proof: a sentence with a wrong number survives
evidence is written in forms the regexes catch (numbers, paths, URLs, [REAL ...] labels, D-ids, quoted output); a bare small integer does not count

input.shape: a long report or note in sentences

name: evidence-only
not_for: checking whether the surviving numbers are right (use numbers-pass)
output: the skeleton of evidence-bearing sentences, the share of text cut, and the longest unsupported stretch

assumes: the genome is a fixed-length numeric vector within bounds
a holdout fitness is passed; evolving on one backtest is a many-trial search that overfits
fitness is cheap enough for population x generations evaluations

input.shape: Python: a fitness(genome)->float to maximise, bounds per gene, Dials, and ideally a holdout fitness

name: evolution-arena
not_for: declaring the champion strategy real - judge it with deflated-sharpe / pbo-overfit on the holdout
output: best genome, best fitness, per-generation history, holdout_gap and the dials used; drift_check gives neutral vs selected fixation rates

assumes: losses are passed as positive numbers (-returns)
observations are roughly iid; volatility clustering biases the tail fit
the threshold choice is stable: rerun at threshold_q 0.90, 0.95 and 0.975, and a big move means the estimate is fragile

input.shape: a return or loss series long enough to have many tail observations (thousands of points), passed as positive losses

name: evt-tail
not_for: a short series with a handful of losses, or a regime question (when the tail changed)
output: Hill tail index xi, a POT fit {u, xi, sigma, n_exceed} with VaR and ES at chosen quantiles, compared with the normal VaR

assumes: inputs are returns with roughly zero mean
one decay rate (span) suits the series; mean-reverting vol clustering needs garch-vol
sizing at bar t uses sizing_vol (lagged), not ewma_vol (includes bar t)

input.shape: a list of periodic returns (not prices)

name: ewma-vol
not_for: a price series passed directly, or a multi-step volatility forecast
output: vol series, one-bar-lagged sizing_vol series, annualized value

assumes: functions have telling names or docstrings - ranking is word overlap
callers use static imports; getattr / importlib / passed-around functions are invisible, so blast radius is a lower bound
the tool files parse with ast

input.shape: the skill library's tool .py files plus a plain-language need, or a skill:module.func id for --impact

name: exaptation-finder
not_for: finding a whole skill for a task (skill-finder)
output: ranked public functions (skill, file, args, doc, returns, score); --impact: caller tiers, tests, docs, blast radius in skills

assumes: attribute directions are right: lower-better is guessed by column name or (given-score mode) by correlation with the score
attributes interact only one at a time; two-attribute interactions are not tested
attributes are numeric and comparable across items

input.shape: a JSON list of items or a CSV with numeric attribute columns, optionally a given score column (--opt score=col)

name: exchange-places
not_for: a ranking whose score uses a direction the tool cannot infer (a wrong direction looks consistent in given-score mode)
output: DOMINANCE and NAME EFFECT inconsistencies, the hinge attribute that flips most pairs, and the count of fragile pairs

assumes: hand-waves show in wording (hedges, intensifiers, absolutes, unnamed authorities) from its word lists
a comparison with any number in its sentence is let through

input.shape: a claim, result write-up or reply about to go to a sharp reader

name: expert-eye
not_for: checking whether the numbers themselves are wrong (use numbers-pass)
output: per sentence the hand-wave category and the question an expert would ask; hand-wave density and the worst sentence

assumes: fake secrets are assigned to secret-named variables, dict keys, setenv or os.environ (api_key, secret, token, *_KEY...) in the same file as the check
leak checks are written as '... not in ...' on those literals; other assertion forms are not seen

input.shape: a folder of Python test files that set fake keys/tokens and assert they do not leak

name: fake-secret-sentinels
not_for: scanning for REAL leaked secrets in a commit - use staged-secret-scan
output: S-SHORT and S-ABSENT lines with file:line and a SUMMARY count; exit 1 when anything is flagged

assumes: claim type is read by regex; a sentence can carry several forms and each gets a refuter
refuters are templates filled from the sentence: they say what to watch, not how to measure it
it never checks a claim against data; the refuters must be pre-registered before looking

input.shape: a thesis, note or result write-up whose sentences make claims (forecasts, causal, numeric, absolute)

name: falsifier-view
not_for: a data table or backtest result to test directly, or a text with no claim sentences
output: per claim a typed refuter (counterexample, missed date, value out of range, effect without cause) and a list of claims nothing could refute

assumes: a synthetic world with the effect planted can be built, or every detector output is VOID
the sketch is causal (value at bar t uses bars <= t), stdlib only, under ~20 s
synthetic-only work stops at REAL = None (UNDERPOWERED), never a live edge

input.shape: a fascination stated as one falsifiable question, built into a stdlib sketch that imports scripts/forge_kit.py

name: fascination-forge
not_for: an already-built strategy wanting a verdict on real data (backtest-verdict, forward-score)
output: a sketch under experiments/sketches/ with SELFTEST PASS, armed / noise_crowning results and a KillLog bin (REAL, KNOWN, NET, COUNTERPARTY, RUIN)

assumes: the fast function reports which path ran
a case exists for each of the four cache states
the slow path is the trusted reference answer

input.shape: a slow function, a fast function returning (answer, 'fast'|'slow'), and cases for clean, incomplete, behind and damaged cache states

name: fast-path-proof
not_for: memoizing a pure function (lru-cache plus clone-check)
output: prove() report ok / failures per case; guard_is_load_bearing True only if removing the validity check breaks the proof

assumes: EVERY p-value computed is included, the dull ones too
each p-value is valid on its own (overlapping returns need HAC, no look-ahead)
BH assumes independent or positively correlated tests; otherwise use BY

input.shape: a list of p-values, one per test run (signals, tickers, buckets), passed in code

name: fdr-control
not_for: deciding whether one particular discovery is real (a 10% FDR list still holds duds), or p-values from a search that hid the losing variants
output: a discovery boolean per test under BH, BY, Holm or Bonferroni, and Storey q-values with pi0, the estimated share of true nulls

assumes: the transient exceptions are listed in retry_on; anything else is treated as a bug and propagates
one step is one fetch: pagination, scheduling and refresh hints are the caller's job
the limiter and breaker live in memory, so a restarted process starts with a full bucket and a closed breaker; the feed's terms were read first

input.shape: a fetch function returning a list of dict rows, a data-intake contract, and store / WAL paths

name: feed-harvest
not_for: a one-off bulk download (use measure-first and data-intake directly)
output: per step a report with status clean / quarantined / rejected / duplicate / fetch_failed / circuit_open / rate_limited, attempts, batch and intake info

assumes: the provider's terms were read and allow scripted access (no Kraken, D74); unreadable terms mean default=False
a real response is captured as a fixture with curl, never invented
the server's cache headers (Cache-Control, Expires, ETag, Retry-After) are the pacing truth; the min_interval is a floor

input.shape: tv-screener's screener/feeds/pollers.py plus a new public feed URL and its captured HTTP response headers

name: feed-poller-add
not_for: a paginated REST harvest or bulk download - use harvest-ceilings / feed-harvest
output: a parser, a registered Source, a fixture test, a live 5 s smoke check; poll_pace gives next delay with reason, conditional headers and a deprecation note

assumes: each snapshot carries its true fetch time and the bar time is the bar OPEN time
snapshots come from fetches already made (no new pulls; D74(c) bans scripted Kraken pulls)
enough observations per age (--min-obs, default 10) and old enough snapshots; otherwise UNKNOWN or NOT SETTLED

input.shape: 2 or more CSV snapshots of one feed's newest bars, each given as file.csv@fetch-time, one bar-open time column plus numeric columns

name: feed-revision-rate
not_for: a single snapshot, or comparing two different vendors' bars (second-source)
output: a table by bar age at fetch (OPEN, 0, 1, 2...) with observations, changed count, rate and largest change, removed bars, and SETTLE AGE N; exit 0 settled, 1 NOT SETTLED/UNKNOWN, 2 bad input

assumes: factors are independent (correlated factors make the band wrong)
each (lo, hi) is an honest 90% belief interval with lo > 0 for log-normal
the total really is a product or sum of products; chained estimates need distance-ladder

input.shape: a dict of factors each a constant, (lo, hi) 90% range, or (lo, hi, normal), via the estimate library call

name: fermi-estimate
not_for: a quantity that has data to bootstrap (use bootstrap-ci for that factor)
output: median, 5-95% band, analytic log-normal cross-check, each factor's share of uncertainty

assumes: samples are evenly spaced
a strong trend is removed first, else its energy floods the low frequencies
for the spectrogram each window holds at least ~4 cycles of the period

input.shape: an evenly spaced numeric series, detrended, holding several cycles of the periods of interest

name: fft-spectrum
not_for: proving a market cycle is real - a peak needs a null test
output: dominant frequencies with period and power; one-sided power spectrum; spectrogram peak period per window

assumes: linking is by exact content words, no stems or synonyms ('bar' and 'bars' do not link)
the seed term follows the theme wanted (default is the top linking keyword; pass --opt seed)
for items, the z threshold (default 1.0) suits the data; a lower z reaches more

input.shape: a text or plan (terms and sentences loop), or an items.json of rows with numeric columns (rows and columns loop)

name: figure-eight
not_for: a text that says the same thing in varied words (the loop closes on the seed sentence)
output: passes until closure, what each pass added, how many sentences or rows the closure reached, and what it never reached

assumes: the subject is the words before the first verb-like token (no parser); unusual sentence shapes get the wrong split
pronouns count as figures and are not resolved

input.shape: a note or plan in plain English sentences

name: figure-ground
not_for: tables, code or bullet fragments without sentence structure
output: words that are only ever ground (and their share of vocabulary), the swapped new figure

assumes: the grid of floors is declared BEFORE looking and kept small (2-3 values per floor); a big grid is a search
same-day trades share shocks, so --cluster date is passed
names already missing from the file (delisted) stay missing - survivorship is not fixed

input.shape: a CSV with one row per trade/event: the excess return, the columns a floor applies to (close, dollar_volume, age) and the entry date

name: filter-sensitivity
not_for: a daily return series of one strategy - it needs per-trade rows with the universe columns
output: a table per cell (n, clusters, mean, t, p, status) and VERDICT FILTER-FRAGILE / ROBUST-SIGNIFICANT / ROBUST-NULL; exit 3 on fragile

assumes: every try was written to a file the glob finds; tries never written stay invisible
the --key set includes every parameter that makes a config distinct, else real tries merge and the count comes out low
Sharpe units match across files, and tries are roughly independent (correlated configs overstate the haircut)

input.shape: a glob of result JSON/JSONL files from a finder or search, plus the dotted keys that define a config's identity

name: finder-tries-counter
not_for: a single pre-registered strategy, or result files that do not record per-config rows
output: evaluations, distinct configs, unscored, claimed trial count, SR0 at claimed vs actual N and the margin of the best; with --n-obs a DSR

assumes: the ask list from literal-execution's parser is read and corrected by hand
evidence is checked for presence only, not truth
the stop hook points at THIS session's ledger; a ledger with no ask table passes freely

input.shape: an ask ledger: finish_check JSON {ask: evidence} or a markdown table with ask, status, blocker columns

name: finish-everything
not_for: proving the claimed evidence is real (pair numbers-pass, receipt-report)
output: rows DONE / NOT DONE / BLOCKED, extras list, finished flag; exit 1 while NOT DONE (stop hook exits 2)

assumes: passive voice is the regular be-verb + participle form (irregular participles are missed)
adjectives like 'is broken' may be misread as passive
a 'by X' phrase names the real actor

input.shape: a report, post-mortem or memo in prose

name: first-person-rewrite
not_for: polishing prose - the rewrite is a pointer, not finished text
output: passive sentences rewritten active with [WHO?] for missing owners, and the count of unowned claims

assumes: the series is ordered oldest first, so the last value is the newest
the fixed log-age weighting is the distortion of interest (no tunable decay)
the series is long enough that recent and old differ

input.shape: a CSV series or list of numbers ordered oldest to newest

name: fisheye
not_for: deciding which view is right (after a regime change the recent view may be the better guide)
output: how many newest bars fill half the view, fisheye vs flat mean (in sd), fisheye vs flat slope with SIGN FLIPS flag, a resample at ages 0, 1, 3, 7, 15...

assumes: the weights are good estimates of each item's load
items are independent and any item may go to either half (no affinity or ordering constraints)

input.shape: a list of numeric weights (work estimates), one per item

name: fission
not_for: an N-way split or splitting items that must stay together
output: {a, b, sum_a, sum_b, imbalance, both_viable} from longest-processing-time greedy; both_viable False when two non-empty halves are impossible

assumes: the first line or heading states the topic; with YAML frontmatter the first line is '---', so pass topic=
5-letter stem matching does not merge unrelated words that share a prefix

input.shape: a document or reply whose title or first line states its topic (or topic= given)

name: fixation-point
not_for: a short text of a few sentences - every content word ties for recurrence
output: the most recurring content word, its sentence count, and ON-TOPIC or DRIFTED versus the stated topic

assumes: the claim is a 'keeps going' trend story; it extrapolates on purpose and is not a forecast
the exponential fit needs every value positive
the absurdity band (k ranges) is a convention; set cap when a real ceiling is known

input.shape: a numeric series (CSV or list) such as a growth count, equity curve, cache size or runtime, with tens of steps

name: flash-forward
not_for: fitting a saturating curve (logistic-growth) or a real forecast with error bars
output: linear and exponential projections and the first step (and multiple of history length) where each becomes absurd: negative, above cap, or beyond k times the observed range

assumes: enough groups for a group-level correlation to mean anything (3 groups rest r on 3 points)
linear relations: Pearson only, outliers can drive r
quantile bins are a sensible collapse when no grouping column is named

input.shape: items JSON or CSV of rows with several numeric columns and optionally a grouping text column

name: flatland
not_for: a time series (use regime-split) or a table with only one numeric column
output: per column-pair collapse: rows r vs groups r tagged FLIPS / VANISHES / APPEARS / AMPLIFIES / holds

assumes: the network is at steady state - internal nodes store nothing
every real source and sink is declared (an undeclared one shows as a leak)
all flows are in one unit

input.shape: a list of (u, v, flow) edges with the sources and sinks named

name: flux-balance
not_for: networks with legitimate buffers or queues at internal nodes
output: {balanced, imbalances{node: inflow - outflow}}

assumes: dates are written in ISO form YYYY-MM-DD; prose dates are not read
a modification time means the content is current (a rewritten old snapshot looks fresh)
a folder has under 5000 files (the scan stops there)

input.shape: a status or notes markdown with ISO dates per section, a data folder (by file mtime), or items.json with a date or age field

name: fog-of-war
not_for: judging whether content is correct, or a folder whose files are regenerated nightly whatever their content
output: each region labelled FRESH / AGING / FOG / NEVER SEEN with its age, fog listed first, counts and the stalest age

assumes: the rule, window and threshold were pre-registered before the run
event times use fixed UTC proxies (CME hours move with US daylight saving; CME crypto went 24/7 in 2026, so pass --until)
controls are matched on the right covariate; an unmatched confound (hour-of-day volatility) can still masquerade as the effect

input.shape: a Binance-style hourly bar folder (or bars plus event times and an outcome function) covering the folklore's era

name: folklore-event-test
not_for: a rule chosen after looking at the same data (the p-value then means nothing)
output: event hit rate vs matched-control null hit rate with one- and two-sided permutation p

assumes: moves are absolute one-step differences; volatility regimes are not modelled
items carry an age column; the age adjustment is a linear fit

input.shape: a price/score series, or items.json with an age column (age, age_days, days, days_ago) and a score column

name: foreshortening
not_for: a regime break - a genuinely new large move after a calm history reads as 'inflation'; use changepoint
output: the recent window's biggest move's full-history percentile and the recency inflation %, or for items the recency slope and demoted items

assumes: the claim's own fields are true; a CLOSED route rests on them unverified (timestamps and variant counts need forward-score or lineage-ledger records)
silence is OPEN: a sparse claim lists many routes, which measures what it leaves unsaid, not that it is wrong
faker costs in rubric.json are judgement, not measurement

input.shape: a claim.json of fields: kind (backtest / forward record / test pass / model metric / data finding), variants_tried, period, preregistered, out_of_sample, shared, deflated, lookahead_checked...

name: forgery-plan
not_for: a prose write-up not yet reduced to claim fields, or proving an effect is real (closing every route only rules out the cheap fakes)
output: every forgery route marked OPEN or CLOSED with its cost and the skill that closes it, and the verdict: the cheapest route still open

assumes: proper nouns are detectable by capitals, CamelCase or acronyms; common sentence openers can slip in
judgments use words from a small English evaluative lexicon (sarcasm missed)
any number counts as evidence, even an irrelevant one

input.shape: a prose verdict, review or note naming people, vendors or sources

name: forget-the-name
not_for: checking whether the evidence that is given is any good
output: judgments sorted name-driven / evidenced / unnamed, name_driven_share, masked noun count

assumes: both files write fields as key: value or JSON that its aliases map (window, alpha, filters, variants, looks)
every fork made in code is also written in the receipt - code-only forks are invisible
disclosed changes are listed under disclosed: or deviations:

input.shape: a pre-registration and a run receipt, each JSON or markdown key: value lines

name: fork-audit
not_for: a run that was never pre-registered
output: per field changes (window shortened / shifted, filters added, alpha loosened, peeking) and verdict UNDISCLOSED FORKS (exit 1) / DISCLOSED DEVIATIONS / clean

assumes: outcomes are binary (continuous returns need GaussianSPRT directly)
each prediction is logged before its outcome is known and after the spec was registered; the spec is not edited later
the ledger stays at thousands of rows (each log re-reads it); the spec hash sits beside the spec, so it stops accidents, not forgers

input.shape: signal specs, timestamped probability predictions and 0/1 outcomes fed through the Pipeline API into a storage folder

name: forward-pipeline
not_for: a backtest or any record logged after the outcomes were known
output: per signal n, scored and look-ahead-excluded counts, hits, SPRT status, p-value, BH discovery, Brier and a recommendation PROMOTE / HOLD / RETIRE / STOP / KEEP LOGGING

assumes: the signal was frozen and registered before any prediction was logged
outcomes come from the settlement/truth store, not typed in by hand
each outcome's known-time is recorded so look-ahead predictions can be excluded

input.shape: a forward JSONL ledger of registered signals (with pre-reg hash) and timestamped predictions, plus outcomes from a truth store

name: forward-score
not_for: scoring an in-sample backtest (EXPLORE numbers never count toward it)
output: refusals for backdated or re-registered writes; an out-of-sample Brier score over predictions made before their outcome was known

assumes: the series is clean and in time order with no NaN (data-hygiene first)
nine early drops tested against one null means a borderline series can be called FOUNDER-DRIVEN by chance

input.shape: a return series (CSV column or list) of at least 4 x blocks points, no NaN

name: founder-effect
not_for: a conclusion that hangs on the most RECENT data - use rear-view-mirror
output: per trim/block drop: value, move, SIGN FLIP, beyond-null; VERDICT FOUNDER-DRIVEN / FRAGILE-EVERYWHERE / ROBUST

assumes: the series is long enough to absorb the warm-up window (about 500 bars at d=0.2 with thresh 1e-4)
an ADF pass is read together with the level weight; on a random walk any d < 0.5 still leaves a random walk inside
the input is a level series (log prices), not returns

input.shape: a log-price series with enough bars to lose a warm-up window (hundreds to thousands of bars)

name: frac-diff
not_for: a returns series that is already stationary, or a short series of a few hundred bars
output: the FFD series (leading None warm-up), and min_d: the smallest d passing ADF with its t-stat, critical value, correlation with the original and level weight table

assumes: framing shows up as words from the paired gain/loss lexicon
a percentage within four words of a framed word is a share of a whole (else complemented wrongly)
word swaps keep grammar acceptable; false frames like right now occur

input.shape: a result write-up, pitch or decision note with gain/loss words and percentages

name: framing-detector
not_for: reversing the whole tone of a text (polarity-flip)
output: per framed sentence GAIN/LOSS counts and the reframed sentence with complemented percentages

assumes: the corpus exists and contains the topic's key terms (absent terms get no chain)
sentence windows are meaningful - Max's uncapitalised prompts can make one prompt one coarse window
one greedy chain per seed is enough (deterministic, not a sample of paths)

input.shape: a short topic text, with Max's MAX_PROMPTS_*.md archive as the corpus

name: free-association
not_for: finding what Max actually said about a topic (prompt-genealogy, transcript-grep)
output: association chains from each key term and the word each lands on (NEW to the text or not); 'no history' terms

assumes: a known-at column exists; without it look-ahead leaks cannot be seen
all times share one comparable format (ISO text or numbers); 10/09/2026 compares wrongly
the cut time t is given (with no time column, row order is the clock)

input.shape: a dated CSV (or items JSON) with a time column and ideally a known_at / published / revised / settled column

name: freeze-frame
not_for: judging a strategy (it only slices the data), or a table with no publication time where the leaks are the question
output: rows dropped as FUTURE or LOOK-AHEAD, frozen vs full mean per numeric column, and each entity's last value at t vs its final value

assumes: both voices print the same key names; NO-COMMON-KEYS is never agreement
the voices are independent: shared code is only detected through command-line files and their local imports (numpy or a sys.path package is not seen)
the tolerance fits the claim (exact for counts, one null draw for Monte Carlo p)

input.shape: two commands (or a saved output and a command) that both print 'key = value' numbers with the same key names

name: fugue-verifier
not_for: two runs of the same script (that is reproduction, use reproduce-before-rejudge)
output: per key agree / DISAGREE, VERDICT CONSONANT or DISSONANT with the first dissonance, and an INDEPENDENCE line (SHARED-CODE); exit 0 / 3 / 4

assumes: the score is a weighted sum of RAW columns, so column units carry hidden weight
the default weights (+1 first column, -1 the rest) match the intent, or --opt weights= is given
one weight at a time is enough; joint distortions are not explored

input.shape: items.json or table.csv of options by numeric columns, with weights (default first column +1, the rest -1)

name: funhouse-mirror
not_for: a ranking by a single metric - with no weights there is nothing to distort
output: robust and fragile conclusions (leader, top half, last place) and, per distortion, what broke and what it became

assumes: one-way doors are found by a heuristic verb list; 'tell' counts as one-way even when harmless
an undo or guard counts only when it is in the same step; an archive two steps earlier is not seen
the plan is split into steps the parser can number

input.shape: a step-by-step plan or text with action verbs (delete, push, land, send, drop) and deferral words (later, TODO, temporary, for now)

name: future-self
not_for: a finished operation's log, or code; it reads plan text only
output: next-week regrets (unguarded one-way doors), next-year regrets (deferred or growing costs), guarded doors, and the step that is the point of no return

assumes: returns are mean zero (or pass demean=True)
the sample is long enough that persistence near 1 is identified
the fit is in-sample and Gaussian; forecasts need an out-of-sample check

input.shape: a return series, at least 20 points and in practice 1000+, via the fit_garch library call

name: garch-vol
not_for: a short series of a few dozen returns or a quick causal vol for sizing (ewma-vol)
output: omega, alpha, beta, persistence, long-run variance, half-life, loglik, next_var; h-step variance forecast

assumes: the gate passes (exit 0) on clean input
the planted old text occurs exactly once in its file
the root can be copied to a temp dir and the gate run there

input.shape: a gates.json registry: per gate a root, a command (exit 0 = pass), source files and one planted fault

name: gate-registry
not_for: measuring a whole test suite's kill rate (mutation-audit)
output: per gate ARMED / DUD / BROKEN / STALE / MISSING-PLANT / AMBIGUOUS-PLANT; status 'ARMED k/n', exit 1 unless all ARMED

assumes: CONFIRMED status came from a real precision gate (candidate-then-gate); a wrong confirm is priced as if real
both venues are priced on the same scale (probability 0..1) and a flat per-side fee stands in for spread and depth
quotes are dense enough: as-of join without interpolation, and z needs at least 4 aligned points

input.shape: pairs.csv (pair_id, venue_a, market_a, venue_b, market_b, status) and quotes.csv (venue, market, ts, price)

name: gated-divergence
not_for: a pair list that has not been through a criteria gate, or deciding to trade (paper-only)
output: per pair OPEN / INSIDE-FEES / STALE / NO-DATA / DUPLICATE-LEG / GATED-OUT with gap, net of fees, z and n; --json

assumes: the stages are listed in true pipeline order; a died_at name not in --stages is refused
each candidate dies at its FIRST rejecting stage only

input.shape: a candidate generator's stage predicates in code, or a JSONL of {id, died_at} lines plus the ordered stage names

name: generator-funnel
not_for: judging whether the survivors are good (it only counts where candidates die)
output: a stage funnel table (entered, killed, passed, kill%, alive%, example rejects) with WALL / DEAD / ERRORS / BOTTLENECK flags; CLI exit 0, 1 a WALL stage, 2 bad input

assumes: slot cue words appear when a slot is answered; a cue word counts as filled even if the sentence does not really answer it
the note fits one of the three shipped genres (incident, lab, recipe)

input.shape: a note or write-up, poured into an incident, lab or recipe template

name: genre-shift
not_for: grading the quality of a postmortem - a filled slot means a cue word appeared, not that it was answered
output: filled and empty slots for the genre, sentences that fit nowhere, and the best-fitting genre

assumes: thresholds are relative (1.5x median nearest-neighbour distance), so every input gets some groups; only the multi-law wholes mean much
columns are equally weighted after z-scoring, so an irrelevant column still pulls items apart
series similarity is only counts of up, down and flat moves

input.shape: a list of items with numeric columns (items.json) or a numeric series file

name: gestalt
not_for: a statistically tested clustering or a table of mostly irrelevant columns
output: groups under proximity, similarity and continuity, the WHOLES the laws agree on, and loners

assumes: both copies change at similar rates; a copy that only grew is ONE-SIDED with no date
r per day comes from a calibration pair of known age or is an honestly stated guess
the copies share an origin (unrelated files give a meaningless date)

input.shape: two copies of the same text file, or two folders of matching files selected by --glob

name: glottochron
not_for: two copies in one git history (speciation reads commits directly)
output: days since split with 95% interval and shared-line share per file, or ONE-SIDED

assumes: one action per sentence in active voice - passive sentences are skipped
the imposing verbs are on its fixed list
REJECT means ask first; context the verb list cannot see decides

input.shape: a rule, message or process draft of actor-verb-receiver sentences or imperative steps

name: golden-rule
not_for: passive-voice reports with no actors (first-person-rewrite first)
output: per action REJECT / OK with the reversed sentence and the consent check

assumes: cards carry an ASSERTIONS block (those without are skipped unless --strict)
the hook list is a heuristic: an OK line can still be wrong; only VAGUE and NO_HOOK are certain
reuse references (file:line) resolve under --root / --key when that check is wanted

input.shape: a plan markdown with per-item cards holding an ASSERTIONS block plus READING / FAILS IF / KILL fields

name: gradable-acceptance
not_for: prose plans with no card structure (nothing is graded) or judging whether an assertion tests the right thing
output: one row per problem (card id, line, NO_HOOK / VAGUE / NO_PLANT / NO_REAL / count bounds / REUSE_BAD) and a summary; exit 0 clean, 1 problems or no card, 2 bad args

assumes: the rootstock's pre and post validators already capture the invariants that matter
the scion's harm shows in its return value (side effects inside it are not caught)

input.shape: a new Python function plus the base pipeline's input and output validator functions

name: graft
not_for: code with no proven validators to inherit (there is no rootstock to graft onto)
output: a wrapped callable that checks input, runs the scion, checks its output, and raises (or returns the on_reject sentinel) on a violation

assumes: the series is long enough that coarse grains still have several blocks; with few blocks the coarse verdicts are noise
the input mode is detected right (levels vs increments) or given with --opt mode=

input.shape: a price or increment series long enough for 4+ non-overlapping blocks at grain 8 (mode auto|levels|increments)

name: granularity-switch
not_for: choosing the right bar size - it reports instability, not which grain is correct
output: per grain (1,2,3,4,6,8) drift sign, up-share, lag-1 autocorr sign, variance ratio; the conclusions marked UNSTABLE with the first grain where they change

assumes: coordinates share comparable units, since attraction uses raw distance squared
masses mean importance; without them every item weighs 1
the bond threshold is calibrated by hand (strongest_bond helps); the result swings with it

input.shape: a dict of item name to coordinate (number or tuple), optionally masses per item, in Python

name: gravity-cluster
not_for: a CSV to cluster from the command line (no file CLI) or high-dimensional data with mixed units
output: clusters, lone_bodies (outliers nothing binds), n_clusters and strongest_bond

assumes: self-copy and install calls sit on one line (a path in one variable and the copy call on the next is missed)
documentation or guard lines naming scheduler commands are flagged and need reading
deliberate copies carry the gray-goo: allow marker

input.shape: a skill library or repo folder of .py, .ps1, .bat, .cmd and .sh files

name: gray-goo-guard
not_for: proving code is safe to run (it is a line regex scan, not a sandbox)
output: SELF-COPY / SELF-SPAWN / INSTALL / OVER-CAP lines with file:line and VERDICT KILL (exit 2) / REVIEW (exit 1) / clean

assumes: red and green comments name the same key (sha, 'wave N', branch)
'failed' in a comment means a red state, not a passing mention
gh is logged in for --live

input.shape: issue #41 comments, live through gh or saved from gh api --paginate

name: green-after-red
not_for: deciding whether something is red now - check git and the checks
output: red comments with no later green / passed / landed / fixed on the same key, newest first, with links

assumes: the block came from tv-guard or the auto-mode classifier, and a block is a decision, not a puzzle
the retry is judged by action class after undoing quote splicing, concatenation and escapes
the honest-equivalent table covers the case; when none fits, the move is to ask Max

input.shape: the exact command or write a guard blocked, plus the retry you intend to run instead

name: guard-respect
not_for: finding what the guard misses or probing variants against it; a guard that looks wrong goes to Max
output: retry_check.py says DISGUISED (exit 1) when the retry is the same action class, encoded, secret-bearing or a near-duplicate, else OK, and prints the honest equivalent

assumes: feeling words are in its ~90-word English lexicon; sarcasm and domain words ('crash' as a market event) are misread
negation sits one word before the feeling word

input.shape: an English verdict, note or plan written right after a result

name: gut-check
not_for: grading the evidence in a text (use skeptic-eye or evidence-only)
output: per sentence FEELING / FACT / MIXED / NEUTRAL with valence and arousal, overall mood and the hottest sentence

assumes: each step has a unique time (duplicates are refused) and finite returns
when each logged return spans h steps, --horizon h is passed; otherwise overlapping returns inflate t
the record was logged forward (no backdating) - the tool does not check provenance

input.shape: a forward record JSONL with a realised return field and a time field (or a text file of returns in time order), at least --min-n rows

name: hac-forward
not_for: a binary hit record - hit rates go to sprt-sequential / forward-pipeline
output: hac-forward: EDGE+ / EDGE- / NAIVE-ONLY / NO EDGE with n, mean, lag, naive t, HAC t, two-sided p, se ratio and effective n; exit 2 on refusal

assumes: lags is set to at least the overlap (horizon - 1); the default plug-in is far too small for long overlaps
no regressor is constant or duplicated (singular designs are rejected) and lengths match
HAC cuts false positives but does not remove them (12% vs nominal 5% in the selftest on persistent predictors)

input.shape: a target series y and one or more equal-length regressor series (time-series rows, e.g. overlapping forward returns vs a predictor)

name: hac-regression
not_for: cross-sectional data with no time order, or a claim from many tried regressions (deflate first)
output: coefficients, OLS and HAC standard errors, HAC t-stats and p-values, R^2

assumes: relevance fades exponentially with one constant half-life
the half-life is chosen from the real timescale on which the thing goes stale

input.shape: ages, values and a half-life (or (time, value) points with now) passed to the library functions

name: half-life
not_for: decay that stops or jumps (a hard expiry, a regime change)
output: decay_weight, remaining value, time_to_floor, recency weighted_mean

assumes: the hand-back reached the transcript (agent-message frame or SubagentHandback tool_use)
the agent id is known (list shows them)
masked output is acceptable - key-shaped strings print as <REDACTED>

input.shape: a session transcript .jsonl (or the session folder with subagents/) and an agent id

name: handback-rescue
not_for: searching transcripts for arbitrary lines (transcript-grep)
output: list: agent ids with hand-back sizes and locations; get: the longest report saved to a file, indent stripped; exit 0 / 1 / 2

assumes: evidence_type labels are honest; the rubric scores what the evidence claims to be
timestamps are given in details (missing ones halve the score; a log not before its outcome scores 0)
the rubric costs are judgement, kept in their checked order

input.shape: an evidence.json list of {claim, evidence_type, details{logged_at, outcome_at, caught, same_code}} items

name: handicap-test
not_for: deciding a claim is right (COSTLY means hard to fake, not true), or evidence whose labels nobody has checked against the records
output: per claim a verdict (COSTLY / CHEAP-ONLY ...), an honesty weight, each item's cost with downgrade notes, and FLAG lines for claims resting only on cheap signals

assumes: the pack has the seven parts in order, with a full path AND a link in the where part
the jobs fit what the reader can actually reach (env_matrix measures it); the checker checks completeness, not whether the jobs are good

input.shape: an info pack markdown for another Claude instance (where things are, what it cannot see, rules, 5-10 jobs, how to hand back, inspirations)

name: handoff-pack
not_for: a session ledger or a status report (it checks a job pack's seven parts)
output: pack_check: PROBLEM lines and exit 1 when parts are missing or out of order, rules over ten or not one-liners, jobs lack ids or a definition of done, or a secret-shaped string appears

assumes: transcripts record Bash tool calls in the standard JSONL format
--skills-root points at the skill library, or adopted tools are not tagged and every shape reads HAND
shape masking (strings, paths, numbers, hashes) keeps script names distinct enough to group

input.shape: a folder of Claude Code session transcripts (JSONL), optionally with subagent transcripts (--sub)

name: hapax-commands
not_for: one session's call log - cross-session recurrence is the point; use transcript-miner for one session

assumes: timestamps sorted and inside [0, T], one stream (no buy/sell cross-excitation)

name: hawkes

name: hdr-view

name: hyperloglog

name: hysteresis
