name: outside-view
not_for: a case with no comparable history
output: shrunk estimate, base rate, r used or measured, case percentile, shrinkage share

assumes: coverage is cue-word presence ('we check' counts as a checklist)
the five fixed trades and their hand-written cue lists are useful prompts for this subject
the text uses ordinary words the cue lists can match

input.shape: a plan or note in plain English prose

name: outsider-council
not_for: an expert review of the subject's own domain (the trades are prompts, not experts)
output: per outsider (chef, pilot, nurse, judge, farmer) coverage share, the missing concerns, the sentence it would interrogate, and the most alarmed outsider

assumes: acronyms are introduced as 'Long Name (ACR)' or 'ACR = ...' (field acronyms the reader knows still flag)
pronouns inside a paragraph have their referent nearby; only paragraph openers are checked

input.shape: a reply, report or doc about to go to someone who was not in the session

name: over-the-shoulder
not_for: an internal note for readers who share the context (most of it will flag)
output: flags per kind (opaque id, undefined acronym, insider name, jargon, dangling opener, pointer to unseen context) and trips per 100 words

assumes: git fetch --prune was run in the repo the pastes talk about
pastes name branches as 'branch @ sha', scopes as 'X/ only', orders as LAND / DO NOT LAND and ids as D-numbers
the files are given oldest first, since the newest paste's order wins

input.shape: pasted cloud packets / work orders saved verbatim as files in send order, checked against a git repo

name: packet-claim-verify
not_for: a peer's numbers or 'tests green' - use peer-verify
output: a table of claim vs state now (MATCH, MOVED, REWRITTEN, GONE, MERGED, OUT OF SCOPE, TAKEN/FREE), the orders in force with overrides, and a NEEDS MAX list; exit 1 when any

assumes: prices are positive levels on one clock; log prices make the bps conversion approximate
everything is in-sample; the cointegration can break, so a holdout re-vet is needed
this pair was not picked as the best of many tested (that needs fdr-control)

input.shape: two positive price-level series on the same clock and length, plus cost inputs (size, adv, sigma_bps, spread_bps, fee_bps)

name: pair-trade-vet
not_for: two return series, or a screen over many pairs without selection correction
output: verdict TRADEABLE-ON-PAPER or not with reasons: hedge ratio, EG ADF t vs 5% crit, spread ADF, half-life, expected reversion bps, round-trip cost bps, net bps

assumes: the splice points sit at the window boundaries chosen with w; a mid-window jump is not seen
in text mode a deliberate topic change also scores as a seam; short paragraphs score high by chance

input.shape: a series CSV cut into windows of w bars, or notes.md with paragraphs separated by blank lines or ---

name: panorama
not_for: finding where inside a window a break happened (changepoint)
output: joins scored by robust z with seams listed (bar indexes or paragraph joins), worst join

assumes: order calls use recognisable shapes (submit / create / place order, /orders, .buy( / .sell()
reviewed simulated lines carry a trailing # paper-only-ok
keys are read only from environment variables

input.shape: a folder or file of source code that might call a broker or order API

name: paper-only
not_for: authorising live trading - only Max, with size and loss cap written down
output: file:line HIGH / MED matches for review; exit 1 on an unacknowledged HIGH

assumes: both bearings are measured from the same baseline axis to the same target
the rays are not parallel (equal bearings are unresolved: target at infinity)
angle errors are small against the parallax angle; far targets amplify them

input.shape: a baseline length and two bearings in degrees from observers at 0 and baseline on one axis

name: parallax
not_for: two noisy estimates of a value that are not geometric bearings (that is a fusion or averaging problem)
output: resolved flag, target (x, y), distance and parallax angle

assumes: shuffled moves are the right null; shuffling kills volatility clustering, so clustered-vol series can look unusual for that reason alone
the pattern is one of its four fixed detectors (streak, double-top, breakout, v-reversal) at fixed thresholds
only one detector is judged (choosing the lowest p among four is multiple testing)

input.shape: a price series file (closes in time order)

name: pareidolia-check
not_for: showing a pattern predicts returns (a low p only says it is unusual for shuffled moves)
output: per detector real count vs shuffle mean, p, and a FACE IN THE CLOUDS label when noise draws it often

assumes: trades are exchangeable; overlapping or clustered trades need a block null first
each pass has enough trades (n >= 20) for the half-split axis to mean anything
only real PASSes (significantly positive means) are judged

input.shape: a CSV of per-trade returns in time order with a pass/strategy column and a return column

name: pass-anatomy
not_for: a pass picked from a big search - it checks shape, not multiple testing; use deflated-sharpe / fdr-control too
output: per pass p base/drop/half/trim, the share of matched null passes that dominate it, and DISTINCT or NULL-LIKE; exit 3 if any NULL-LIKE

assumes: both versions are about the same subject; it cannot tell a changed mind from a changed subject
topics are single keywords from each side's top 25; a synonym swap shows as dropped plus new, not shifted
without a separator the file is split in half, which may not match versions

input.shape: two versions of a statement on one subject (two files, or one file split at a --- or === line)

name: past-self
not_for: a line-by-line diff of code or a single version with no older one
output: per shared topic SHIFTED lines (polarity, certainty, numbers changed), dropped and new topics, and one drift score

assumes: the paste is saved to a file or piped intact before checking
Max's stated length or ending is passed with --expect-lines / --expect-end when known
a pasted-text placeholder means the content never arrived

input.shape: a pasted text saved to a file, or an inbox file, optionally with the expected line count or ending

name: paste-receipt
not_for: checking that the content of the paste is correct
output: RECEIVED: chars, lines, sha256 prefix, first and last line, truncation signs PLACEHOLDER / MARKER / FENCE / EXPECT / WEAK; exit 0 clean, 1 strong sign

assumes: the matrix holds every candidate tried, not a pre-filtered set
blocks is even and blocks are long relative to autocorrelation
selection by mean return per column is the selection actually used (adapt _score otherwise)

input.shape: a returns matrix: rows = time, columns = every candidate tried in the search

name: pbo-overfit
not_for: one strategy with no record of the search behind it
output: {pbo, n_splits, median_logit}

assumes: claims sit where the matcher looks: code spans, from-imports, 'selftest n/n' counts, description clauses before 'Use this'
the documented code ships in the skill folder (code in another repo is flagged)
selftests print PASS/FAIL lines; word overlap is only a weak test of a capability

input.shape: the skill library: SKILL.md files with the tool scripts shipped in each folder

name: peacock-tail
not_for: doc-only skills (left out) or deciding a flagged clause is false (a flag is a prompt to look)
output: per skill over-claim score (2 per missing function, 3 per wrong count, 1 per unbacked clause) with each flag, ranked; --run executes every selftest

assumes: the ownership map is current (a named owner's session may have ended: check ListAgents first)
claims name every file to create and every file promised not to touch
a peer's request is not authorisation; settings, CLAUDE.md and guard edits are refused

input.shape: a list of file paths to edit plus an ownership map of globs to session names (from claims on #41)

name: peer-handoff
not_for: merging a finished cloud branch (use merge-cloud-branch)
output: plan_edits: MINE / PEER:<name> / UNOWNED per path; a claim message; verify_claim lists files that broke the claim; peer_request_refusals lists refused paths

assumes: each claim is given a command that reproduces it; claims without one stay UNBACKED
the peer's commands are read before they are run (they run through the shell)
expectations use the supported forms (rc=0, re:, num:key=value~tol, pytest:N)

input.shape: a peer session's post (numbers, 'tests green'), then a claims file of label :: command :: expectation lines

name: peer-verify
not_for: branch@sha and decision-id claims - use packet-claim-verify / landing-inbox
output: per claim VERIFIED / CONTRADICTED / UNBACKED / UNRUNNABLE and an ACT or HOLD line

assumes: the pen CLI (python -m tv_core.writer, run in the Autotrade root) is reachable and prints a claim id; with no claim id it exits 4
the work is ONE command; a multi-step landing needs skills-land or land-a-change around the whole sequence
the command runs without a shell (no pipes, redirects or && inside it)

input.shape: one command to run under the writer pen (argv after --), with a pen label and optional timeout and cwd

name: pen-run
not_for: read-only commands that need no pen, or waiting for a held pen (it never waits, retries or forces)
output: a receipt (command, exit code, seconds, claim id, released or RELEASE FAILED); exit 3 with the holder when the pen is held, 124 timeout, 130 Ctrl-C, 127 missing binary

assumes: rank 1 is the largest value; for costs read the ranking upside down
denominators are non-zero and one-signed (else skipped)
a small noisy denominator can make an item lead by accident

input.shape: items JSON or CSV with several numeric columns per item

name: per-capita
not_for: columns whose ratio has no meaning (dividing by an id or a date)
output: per value/denominator view: leader change, Spearman rank agreement with raw, biggest mover; skipped denominators

assumes: edges are marked (parentheses, note / PS / footnote lines, etc, also, by the way, the last line)
capitalised one-off words are names - emphasis capitals leak in
the file is not bullet-heavy with * (those read as note lines)

input.shape: a doc, memo or reply

name: peripheral-vision
not_for: judging which edge item matters
output: edge items listed by kind (parenthetical, note, trailing, aside, last line, one-off name)

assumes: blockers are written with its phrases (blocked by, waiting on, can't, depends on, missing, until...)
the per-class probe table points at the right kind of look, not the exact command
hidden downstream work is found by shared words (over- or under-count)

input.shape: a status note or plan that names blockers ('blocked by', 'waiting on', 'requires', 'until')

name: periscope
not_for: a text whose blockers are implicit, or as permission to probe a forbidden source (D71 rules still bind)
output: each blocker with its class, what it hides, and the cheapest probe with a cost, ranked cheapest first

assumes: the versions form one line of development (a branching history has no single good order)
lines appear, persist and vanish (contiguity); reverts and merges show as broken features
an --anchor names the oldest copy, since seriation cannot tell first from last

input.shape: a folder or list of undated copies or versions of one file (up to 400), or a 0/1 presence matrix CSV

name: petrie-seriation
not_for: dated versions or a git history (read the dates or the log instead)
output: the most likely order, Petrie contiguity score vs given order and random orders, and the broken features

assumes: samples are evenly spaced so phase = index mod period
the trend is roughly linear; a curved trend shows up as a fake long period
the scan p-value covers the period scan only, not earlier choices of series and window

input.shape: an evenly spaced series (CSV) covering many cycles of the suspected period (hourly for 24, daily for 7)

name: phase-fold
not_for: a tradable seasonality claim - a fold is a hypothesis; follow with seasonality-test
output: FOLD period P (scanned range, scan p): cycles, R^2, F, average cycle shape with per-phase spread, peak and trough phase

assumes: the inputs are genuine phases; raw signals must be turned into phases first
each series is oscillatory with a meaningful cycle; trending or noise series give meaningless phases
the 0.9 lock threshold suits the use; PLV is a coherence, not a significance test

input.shape: two equal-length PHASE sequences in radians (from a Hilbert transform or cycle detection), not raw prices

name: phase-lock
not_for: two raw price or return series (correlation or cointegration), or one series's own periodicity
output: PLV in 0..1 and {plv, locked, threshold}

assumes: the vocabulary is large and homogeneous enough to have letter patterns (a few names give a noisy norm)
new tokens belong to the same naming family as the vocabulary
an assumed 40-symbol alphabet covers the characters used

input.shape: a vocabulary of names (word list or a known CSV header) plus new tokens (args or a new CSV header)

name: phonotactic-check
not_for: checking a field's values or types (schema-contract)
output: per token KNOWN / NATIVE / FOREIGN with bits and z, nearest known name and possible typo hint; exit 1 if any FOREIGN

assumes: each parent has several words to cross at
raw candidates are wanted - some children are ungrammatical
crossing at word boundaries is enough (no reordering or inflection)

input.shape: two parent phrases or sentences

name: phrase-sex
not_for: blending single words (word-sex) or editing a phrase
output: ranked child phrases, each carrying words from both parents

assumes: about 40 nodes or fewer (dense O(n^3) solve per step)
straight-line Euclidean length is the link cost unless your own edges are passed
mu, I0, prune and steps are swept; it is a heuristic with no optimality guarantee

input.shape: positioned nodes (x, y) and an optional candidate edge list, passed in code

name: physarum
not_for: an exact optimal network problem or hundreds of nodes
output: a grown network's edges with total length, connectedness, fault tolerance and mean stretch, compared with the MST and the full candidate graph

assumes: the whole's verdict (sign of the net move, or keyword verdict for text) is itself meaningful; if the whole is noise, agreement means nothing
peek width and count (default 40 peeks of 1/8) match the quick look being judged

input.shape: a price or value series file (or a text, sampled by sentences)

name: pinhole
not_for: deciding whether the whole series has a real trend (use signal-nulls)
output: stability (share of peeks agreeing with the whole), spread and extremes of peek moves

assumes: the jargon terms are in glossary.json; unknown jargon passes silently
a gloss counts only right beside the term (parentheses, dash or colon)

input.shape: a draft message or report to Max containing git, pen, decision or statistics words

name: plain-terms
not_for: learning what MAX's words mean - that is max-lexicon
output: each unexplained term with its position and a suggested plain gloss; explain(term) adds an analogy

assumes: codes match 1-3 capitals plus digits; codes of other shapes are not checked
bare path citations resolve only through the --prefix map to the right repo; new files must be marked new/creates on the line
a resolved citation proves the file and line exist, not that the line says what the plan claims

input.shape: a plan markdown file with section pointers (§x.y), item/card ids, codes like PG10 and backticked path:line citations, plus the repo root and path prefixes

name: plan-closure
not_for: judging whether the plan's content is right, or a prose note with no ids or citations
output: counts and lines per class SECTION_REF, CARD_ID, CODE, CITATION (open) and CREATED; CLOSED or exit 1 while any open reference remains

assumes: the plan's items are first transcribed by hand into items.json
git fetch ran first and remote refs are used
a defect pattern is text the fix must remove; a reworded line reads GONE

input.shape: items.json listing a plan's branch items (repo, branch, base) and defect items (repo, ref, path, pattern)

name: plan-vs-git
not_for: a plan.md passed directly, or proving a LANDED branch works on its base
output: per item LANDED / OPEN / GONE / MISSING with evidence and file:line for OPEN defects

assumes: each plant's old text occurs exactly once in its file (else MISSING / AMBIGUOUS)
the unplanted copy's tests pass (else BASELINE_RED)
the repo can be copied to a temp dir

input.shape: a plant manifest (file, old text, new text, test command per file) and the repo root

name: plant-ledger
not_for: auto-generated operator mutants (mutation-audit)
output: per plant KILLED / SURVIVED / MISSING / TIMEOUT / BASELINE_RED; a chained ledger line; RATCHET BROKEN exit 2 on a falling kill count

assumes: the tree is committed and no other session is editing the files (a crash would not restore)
each 'old' text is present (first occurrence used; MISSING otherwise) and the baseline tests are green
imported modules are recompiled fresh (stale .pyc can fake a verdict; wrap with pyc_fresh.py)

input.shape: a module and its tests, a cases.json of {file, old, new} mutations and the test command after --

name: plant-the-bug
not_for: measuring a whole selftest's kill rate automatically (mutation-audit) or a test that is red before anything is planted (BASELINE_RED: clear its oracle first)
output: KILLED / SURVIVED / MISSING / TIMEOUT per case and 'N planted bugs: K killed, S survived, M missing' (exit 0 only when all killed); survivor_court gives rulings and the 'N of N caught, M equivalent' line

assumes: each finding has a real evidence tier (EXPLORE / forward-scored / live) and receipt; an EXPLORE lead is not described as proven
the data source, tier/API, harvest path and cost are known for each play
edge, tradability, cost and effort numbers exist to rank by

input.shape: a set of research findings with evidence tiers and receipts, turned into play dicts with the six parts

name: playbook-from-results
not_for: a single finding with no data path or cost (it is a diary entry, not a play)
output: a ranked, phased dossier of plays; validate() gives {valid, missing, problems}, rank() orders valid plays by (edge x tradability) / (cost + effort)

assumes: the tone sits in lexicon words (about 40 valenced and 12 direction pairs); other words do not flip
context is ignored: 'not bad' becomes 'not good' and idioms flip word by word

input.shape: a verdict note or report with evaluative words (good/bad, rose/fell, never/always)

name: polarity-flip
not_for: checking whether the verdict is right - it reverses tone, it does not test facts
output: each flipped sentence with valence before and after, the overall valence balance, and sentences with no valence

assumes: skills declare neighbours in 'Pairs with' lines; pairs with zero shared neighbourhood are never proposed
already-crossed pairs are passed via --crossed or detectable from 'merged from / hybrid of' text
description similarity is TF-IDF words, so hub skills many others pair with dominate the top

input.shape: a skill library folder of SKILL.md files with descriptions and 'Pairs with' lines; optional crossed pairs and a candidate subset

name: pollinator-routing
not_for: picking a skill for a task (skill-finder) or a library without Pairs-with lines
output: the top skill pairs to cross with score (1 - similarity) x log2(1 + shared neighbourhood) and a reason

assumes: the copies are independent (shared bug or shared feed defeats the vote)
outputs are numbers for median or discrete labels for majority
N times the work is affordable for this step

input.shape: several callables (implementations, seeds, feeds) and one input, via express()

name: polyploid
not_for: copies that share the same underlying source or code path
output: value, ploidy, survived, failed; raises if every copy fails

assumes: at least ~200 returns (thousands before a 99% ES is trustworthy)
losses are roughly i.i.d. for the EVT tail - filter vol clusters first
one strategy only - no cross-asset correlation

input.shape: one strategy's per-bar return series

name: position-sizer
not_for: a portfolio of correlated assets (risk-parity, cov-shrinkage)
output: size, the binding constraint (vol / kelly / tail / leverage), each candidate, stats; size_from_ruin: size, prob, size_above

assumes: each lens imports pov_core and returns the shared view record
each lens selftest prints at least 6 PASS lines with a planted case
distinctness is judged on the shared PROBES only (0.8 token-shingle Jaccard)

input.shape: the point-of-view lens skills: tools that import pov_core and define apply(subject, kind=None, **opts)

name: pov-core
not_for: deciding what is true about a subject (a lens finding is a question, not a verdict)
output: shared helpers and load_subject; ratify.py prints lenses not ratified with the failing rule R1-R4 and counts, appending to RATIFIED.jsonl

assumes: a quantity's base period comes from nearby words; with no period word it is taken as per trade
trades_per_day and days_per_year fit the strategy (defaults 10 and 252)
scaling is linear plus one compounding-cost line; a positive percent is still shown as a cost

input.shape: a text that quotes costs or edges (bps, %, $) or a series of steps

name: powers-of-ten
not_for: computing realised P&L or compounding over many steps (use long-now)
output: each quantity at per-trade / day / year / decade, the scale where it turns material (100 bps or $1,000), and a compounding-cost line

assumes: the pre-reg and the frozen code are COMMITTED to git before the result exists (check refuses an uncommitted pre-reg)
every bar is numeric and names its exact statistic; a prose bar is not a test
the result file's commit time reflects when it was produced (anti-backdating compares git times)

input.shape: a PREREG_<name>_<date>.md with hypotheses, numeric bars, failure controls and multiplicity, plus the frozen scoring script and later a result file

name: pre-register
not_for: an exploratory run with no bar - registration only means something before the number exists
output: new: a PREREG template; freeze: sha256 of the scoring code; check: pass, or exit 1 when the result predates or lacks a committed pre-reg

assumes: the function accepts both Python ints and floats and returns comparable results
the safe limit is sampled evidence ('no difference seen in N samples'), not proof of exactness
the function is pure and cheap enough for hundreds of calls per band

input.shape: an importable numeric function as mod.py:func taking a list of n numbers (or a built-in --op), and a band range around 2**53

name: precision-domain
not_for: float rounding of non-integer inputs (tolerance-edge) or functions that only take floats
output: a table per exponent band (tried, differ, errors, first counterexample) and SAFE LIMIT 2**k; --emit prints a guard and a pytest test

assumes: the repo registers tests in tests.json by base function name (parametrized ids are checked elsewhere)
ruff is installed (else LINT SKIP)
generated-file rules are declared in .precommit_bundle.json or --generated

input.shape: a repo with staged changes, tests.json and optionally .precommit_bundle.json generated-file rules

name: precommit-bundle
not_for: checking the commit message's numbers (numbers-pass) or replacing the project's full check
output: PASS/FAIL/SKIP lines MARKERS, TESTS, LINT, GENERATED, TREE and commit BLOCKED or ok; exit 0 pass, 1 blocked, 2 bad args

assumes: signals were known at their bar (no look-ahead)
k and q are fixed once - scanning several is another search to count
one-bar outcomes, since multi-bar outcomes cluster

input.shape: an outcome (return) series plus named boolean signal series of the same length

name: precursor-scan
not_for: a tested edge - survivors go to pre-register and forward-score
output: per signal lift with base rate, bootstrap CI, circular-shift p and BH survival, labelled HYPOTHESIS

assumes: the prediction is written before the run (the tool cannot enforce it)
the outcome is decidable by exit code (pass/fail) or recorded by hand
about 20 resolved predictions per kind before the Brier score means much

input.shape: a command, check or claim about to be run, with the expected outcome, probability, seconds and count

name: predict-then-run
not_for: grading market forecasts (calibration-check) or predictions written after the result was seen
output: a prediction id, HIT / MISS per run, Brier and calibration buckets per kind, runtime log2 bias, count accuracy, and a surprise log with rule candidates

assumes: the pre-reg is committed in git with no uncommitted edits
every frozen code file is listed with pre-register's sha256 line format and still hashes the same
results land in a --watch folder so outputs can be receipted and audited

input.shape: a scoring command plus a committed pre-registration markdown with 'path sha256: hex' frozen-code lines, and a receipts JSONL

name: prereg-everywhere
not_for: writing the hypothesis itself (use pre-register first)
output: run: REFUSED (exit 2) or runs the command and appends a receipt row; audit: REGISTERED / UNREGISTERED / CHANGED-SINCE per result file

assumes: urgency shows in words (asap, now, tonight), exclamation marks and shouted words; acronyms are excluded
'now'/'today' are often plain time words, so single hits are weak

input.shape: a prompt, incident thread or go-live note with decisions in it

name: pressure-marker
not_for: real deadlines - a calm sentence can still sit on a hard deadline
output: pressure score per sentence, PRESSURED DECISION lines (score, urgent words, bangs, shouted), and the pressure trend

assumes: triggers are found by regex, not a grammar; the quoted clause is the comma-bounded span, rough in long sentences
definite descriptions are flagged on first mention and generic uses ('the market') show up too
it lists assumptions only; judging whether one is false is another skill's job

input.shape: a question, claim or note in English prose

name: presupposition-scan
not_for: deciding whether a premise is false (smuggled-premise, skeptic-eye) or non-English text
output: each trigger with its type (iterative, continuation, change-of-state, factive, scalar, additive, why-question, comparative, definite) and the background claim it takes for granted

assumes: at least about 8 sentences, or the baseline is noisy
reuse is by 5-letter stems; synonyms (vol vs volatility) are separate
topic words in a focused note steer by design, so STEERING means check, not bias

input.shape: a brief, prompt or research note of about 8 or more sentences

name: priming-detector
not_for: numeric anchoring of estimates (anchoring-detector)
output: opening size, share of later units reusing an opening concept, STEERING primes, UNPRIMED units

assumes: the antipattern has a regex signature
deliberate uses carry the prion-ok marker
min_hosts suits how widely it must spread to count

input.shape: a set of source files and a regex signature of the bad pattern

name: prion-guard
not_for: a one-off bug or a pattern with no regex signature
output: {infected, count, outbreak, min_hosts}

assumes: the total is additive (sums or weight*value sums); ratios like a portfolio Sharpe do not split
the right column is chosen with --opt col= (and weight= if needed)
shares are of the gross, so offsetting parts appear rather than cancel

input.shape: items.json or a CSV with a numeric contribution column (--opt col=), or a series split into segments

name: prism
not_for: non-additive totals such as a Sharpe or a ratio (use shapley-potluck)
output: total, gross, parts ordered by size with shares and cumulative share, parts needed for 80%, effective contributors, parts pulling against the total; gross up and down for a series

assumes: the target function is importable and callable with JSON-expressible arguments
the spec is written with the Write tool (backslash paths break in heredocs)
bisect only shrinks the probe's first list argument

input.shape: a JSON probe spec naming a target module.py:func (or pkg.mod:func) and one probe per edge input, with optional expectations

name: probe-kit
not_for: outside HTTP APIs (use api-probe)
output: a table per probe of input, returned value and verdict OK / FAIL / SEEN; --record writes a golden fixture; --bisect prints the smallest failing input; exit 0 / 1 / 2

assumes: process listing is available (Get-CimInstance on Windows, ps elsewhere)
--pen-chain points at the current writer chain so the pen holder is named
parent chains are intact; a process whose ancestor is gone is labelled ORPHAN

input.shape: the live process table of this machine (or a saved masked snapshot via --from), with optionally the writer chain file

name: process-owner-map
not_for: deciding if a known job is stuck - use long-job's is_stuck.py
output: free RAM line, pen pid, and per process pid, ppid, MB, start time, owner (PEN-HOLDER, SCHEDULED-TASK, SESSION:<pid>, ORPHAN, OTHER) and masked command; never ends a process

assumes: mental states are written with the verbs it knows (wants, thinks, believes); 'Max is keen on' is missed
evidence is a marker (quote, said, asked, source label), found but not checked against the source
first person and 'you need' are directives and skipped

input.shape: a handoff, mailbox post, memory file or brief that says what Max, users or other sessions want, think or believe

name: projection-check
not_for: checking that a quote really says what is claimed (question-not-ruling's checker) or texts with no claims about others
output: each claim about another's mind marked EVIDENCED or PROJECTED with the agent and verb

assumes: equal weights across metrics (weight sensitivity needs funhouse-mirror)
lower-is-better columns are recognised by name (drawdown, cost, vol...) or listed with --opt lower=
more than about 3 items, or tau takes few values and only leader changes are readable

input.shape: items JSON or CSV of items with several numeric metric columns to combine into one score

name: projection-shift
not_for: choosing the metric weights themselves
output: leader and order under z-score, min-max, rank and pct-of-max, worst-pair Kendall tau, count of distinct leaders

assumes: promises are phrased I'll / I will / next I / Next steps / say go and I'll
kept work reuses the promise's rare words or file names (heuristic token overlap)
subagent work came back into the main transcript

input.shape: one Claude Code session transcript .jsonl

name: promise-ledger
not_for: auditing Max's asks (finish-everything)
output: per promise KEPT / RELEASED / NO EVIDENCE / UNCHECKABLE with pointers; open promises crossing compactions; --offers do-next queue

name: skill-maestro
not_for: a task Claude can plainly do in one step (triage says SKIP or QUICK and answers in a few lines), or picking a model or a tool outside the skill library
output: a scored pool and 1 to 22 picks by meaning and purpose, each with its command and its survey verdict; the prompt's MODE with how to use the picks and up to four ASK FIRST questions with defaults; context lines, an AGENDA by phase, FIRST MOVE and STAY INSIDE; ledger receipts for read/try/fit/rate

assumes: the old description routes to the host under skill-finder's TF-IDF (else Refused, nothing written)
no tool file name in OLD collides with one in HOST
repointing is a whole-word replace in SKILL.md and .py only; sentences need reading in the dry run

input.shape: a skills root with an OLD skill folder to fold into a named HOST skill folder

name: skill-retire
not_for: deleting a skill outright with no host to absorb it
output: dry run REPOINT and plan lines; with --apply archive, moved tools, merged section, new description, verified flag; exit 0 planned/done, 1 refused

assumes: the same folder name in each root is the same skill (a renamed copy shows as two MISSING)
a skill folder has a SKILL.md (folders without one are ignored)
the newest copy is only a proposal - when both sides changed, the merge is by hand

input.shape: two or more skill library roots

name: skill-sync-audit
not_for: whether the skills' tools work (skill-health)
output: per skill SAME / EOL-ONLY / DRIFTED / MISSING with differing files; summary; exit 1 on drift or missing

assumes: each SKILL.md description's first sentence works as a 'reach for this when' line
family placement comes from a curated map; new skills fall to a keyword fallback or Other
a skill is [T] when its folder ships a script

input.shape: a skills root folder of <name>/SKILL.md files

name: skills-index
not_for: finding the right skill for a stated need (skill-finder) or checking skills work (skill-health)
output: a regenerated INDEX.md grouping every skill by family with [T]/[D] marks and a one-line reach-for-this

assumes: the clone is a dedicated sync clone, not the shared checkout (the mirror replaces .claude/skills wholesale)
the source holds every skill the clone should keep; project-only skills in the clone are refused unless --allow-remove names them
the pen can be claimed and staged-secret-scan findings are fixed or waived with a reason

input.shape: the global skills folder (~/.claude/skills) and a dedicated repo sync clone with .claude/skills

name: skills-land
not_for: landing project code changes (use land-a-change)
output: dry run: folders added / changed / removed and scan result; --land claims the pen, mirrors, stages, scans, commits, pushes, releases; exit 0 / 2 / 3 refused by scan / 4 pen refused / 5 git step or removal guard

assumes: the runs were saved to files; console-only runs are invisible
-rs summaries give file:line of the skip call, not test ids, and never list passes (reported as no-pass-evidence)
files under 50 MB that look like pytest output

input.shape: saved pytest output (-rs/-rA/-v text) or JUnit XML files across many runs, as folders or globs

name: skip-reason-ledger
not_for: a single run's output - permanence needs several recorded runs
output: skip reasons with counts and weights, and ALWAYS-SKIPPED tests (skipped in every run, >= min-runs, never passed) with evidence grade

assumes: the text is long enough that the correct form of a typo appears 3+ times; rarer typos are invisible
a rare real word one edit from a frequent word can be flagged as a typo
sentence splitting is pov-core's and can break on unusual punctuation

input.shape: a long fast-written prompt, prompt archive or note (thousands of words help, since its own vocabulary is the dictionary)

name: slip-detector
not_for: spell-checking a short text or code identifiers
output: slips (typo with its frequent twin, doubled word, self-correction), slips per 100 words, and RUSHED sentences where slips cluster

assumes: the event of interest is the single largest step; other events need the series cut around them
interpolated frames add no information

input.shape: a price, latency or runtime series CSV with one dominant jump

name: slow-motion
not_for: forecasting how long a future crash recovery takes
output: event bar and size, onset length, peak bar, half and full recovery bars, in/out rates, asymmetry

assumes: even consecutive panels are meaningful slices (regime breaks fall where they fall)
the series is long enough that each of up to 8 panels holds well over 3 points
a least-squares slope and a mean step describe each panel

input.shape: one numeric series long enough for 8 panels of 3+ points

name: small-multiples
not_for: regime-based cuts (regime-split)
output: whole-sample slope, panel agreement per split, dissenting panels

assumes: numbers sit right after the metric name ('Sharpe 3.8'); 'Sharpe, net of costs, came to 3.5' is missed
too-good markers are the fixed thresholds (Sharpe > 3, win rate >= 80%, zero drawdown, guaranteed...)
quiet fraud has no markers, so 'no smell' is not 'clean'

input.shape: a backtest note, vendor pitch or result text, or a table / items.json with metric columns

name: smell-test
not_for: certifying a modest-looking result (overfitting with Sharpe 1.5 has no smell)
output: flags with smell points (3 almost never real, 2 rare, 1 check), the usual cause, and a verdict SMELLS / check it / no smell

assumes: each horn's quote is copied verbatim from the source (case and spacing aside); paraphrases fail
every bridge premise you added is listed honestly
whether a quote actually forces its horn is judged by reading (no shared words is flagged 'check by eye')

input.shape: the source text plus an alleged contradiction written as two horns, each with a claim and an exact quote, and any bridge premises

name: smuggled-premise
not_for: finding contradictions in a text from scratch (it tests one alleged contradiction)
output: THEIRS / YOURS / UNSUPPORTED with reasons per horn

assumes: no single extreme outlier squeezes the rest into a few notes (min-max scaling); log or clip first
series longer than max_bars may be thinned by stride

input.shape: a numeric series file (close.csv), up to max_bars values

name: sonify
not_for: evidence of anything - hearing a pattern is not a test
output: a mono 16-bit WAV file (path), its length, the pitch range and the loudest leaps

assumes: only list items count as claims; prose paragraphs are not checked
the premise check (a FABRICATED item used as a claim's premise) is word overlap, so flags need a read
a REAL label's source is present but not verified

input.shape: a markdown list of ideas or claims, each list item ending in [REAL: source], [IMAGINED] or [FABRICATED]

name: source-labels
not_for: deciding which of Max's clauses are orders or questions (question-not-ruling) or prose with no list items
output: claims with counts per label, issues (unlabelled, REAL without a source, FABRICATED as premise) and ok

assumes: conflicts are textual and per file; INTERFERTILE means git can merge, not that the build works
the hybrid-max and isolated-days thresholds fit this repo; age alone makes a branch ISOLATED
git 2.38+ for merge-tree --write-tree (legacy fallback is less precise)

input.shape: a repo and two refs (branches) to compare

name: speciation
not_for: two copies of a file with no shared git history (glottochron)
output: ahead, behind, days diverged, files touched on both sides, trial-merge conflict list, isolation trend, verdict INTERFERTILE / HYBRID ZONE / ISOLATED with why

assumes: each command's output is deterministic once the declared volatile lines are stripped
the baseline is declared and committed before the first code edit
the commands are Python children that can report CPU seconds at exit (process_time), run N >= 3 times

input.shape: a program plus bench.json naming the commands to benchmark, a target ratio and volatile-line regexes

name: speed-proof
not_for: code with nondeterministic output
output: baseline and candidate JSON with CPU seconds (min of N) and fingerprints; compare IDENTICAL plus ratio, exit non-zero otherwise

assumes: the files sit under --root so paths stay relative
no file holds a secret (the check matches known key shapes only; it is a backstop)
the receiver re-maps every PORTABILITY machine path before acting

input.shape: a momentum THREAD.md plus the files a peer needs (relative to --root), or a packed .spore.json to check or germinate

name: spore-handoff
not_for: files larger than the caps, or copying the files into a project (a deliberate human step)
output: a JSON spore with per-file sha256; check gives OK per file and VIABLE / DEAD with CORRUPT and UNSAFE-PATH entries; germinate restores exact bytes into a new temp dir

assumes: mass is the sum of absolute values (fits sizes and counts; only roughly fits signed scores like Sharpe)
you know for each other attribute whether its max or min is good

input.shape: items (JSON or CSV) with one ranking attribute and other numeric attributes

name: spotlight
not_for: testing whether the top of a ranking is significant (use model-confidence-set)
output: the lit top-k, the share of total mass in the dark, and unlit items holding the max or min of other attributes

assumes: p0, p1, alpha, beta and max_n were pre-registered before the first trade
observations are independent from a fixed distribution; overlapping positions or a regime change break the guarantees
for GaussianSPRT, sigma comes from history, not the forward data

input.shape: forward results arriving one by one: wins/losses (Bernoulli) or per-trade returns (Gaussian, known sigma); Python API

name: sprt-sequential
not_for: a backtest scored all at once - sequential stopping is for forward data arriving over time
output: decision accept_h1 (edge) / accept_h0 (no edge) / inconclusive (hit max_n) / continue, with the log-likelihood ratio

assumes: word frequency stands for importance; a key point said once plainly can be lost
the result is extractive telegraphese to show emphasis, not a written summary
sentence splitting is pov-core's and can break on unusual punctuation

input.shape: a long note or report in prose, squashed to a word budget n

name: squash
not_for: writing a summary to send (token-thrift, plain-terms) or a data table
output: the squashed text at n words, sentences SURVIVED / BRUISED / LOST and the numbers dropped

assumes: the shape is one of five (up, down, U, cap, flat); S-curves or double dips are misread
the tolerance scales with the series' spread, so a small steady drift in a noisy series reads flat

input.shape: one numeric series (file or list)

name: squint
not_for: detecting where or whether a significant change happened
output: one shape word: up / down / U / cap / flat

assumes: secrets have one of its key shapes (AWS, GitHub, sk-, Slack, Google, PEM, Telegram, long secret-named literals) - a bare random string under an innocuous name is missed
submodule changes are scanned inside each submodule (the root shows them as SKIPPED no blob)
the files to push are already staged (default) or the commit range is given - the working tree is not what is read

input.shape: a repo with staged changes, a commit range, or plain paths

name: staged-secret-scan
not_for: a secret that already reached a pushed commit - rotate the key, a scan cannot unpush it
output: every finding masked (first two characters and length) with file and line; 'STAGED SCAN: N file(s), k skipped, M finding(s)'; exit 1 on any finding, 2 if git fails

assumes: evidence sits on the same line as the claim (a sha, a receipts/ path, rc=0, 'run on', a #41 link)
only the listed claim words count; lower-case 'done', conditional or negated lines are skipped
a cited sha is taken at face value; whether it backs the claim is not checked

input.shape: a plan or report markdown with status words (MET, DONE, PASSED, green, verified, fixed, landed) in tables or lines

name: status-honesty
not_for: verifying that the cited evidence proves the claim (a sha that shows less still passes)
output: each unsupported claim word with its line and the honest word to use (FOUND / RECORDED / OPEN)

assumes: the text itself holds the evidence and mechanisms (it never invents them)
softening absolutes word by word is acceptable ('all' becomes 'most' even when literally true)

input.shape: an opposing argument or plan with at least 2 claims

name: steelman
not_for: a one-claim text or one whose strength lies in evidence elsewhere
output: claims scored for strength (number, mechanism, source, specificity), repairs made, and the rebuilt strongest version from the top claims

assumes: use events are reported as deposits and evaporation is ticked on a regular schedule
the deposit amount and evaporation rate are tuned to how fast attention should fade

input.shape: Python: a trail dict of item -> strength updated by use events and periodic evaporation ticks

name: stigmergy
not_for: an all-time usage count - it forgets by design
output: a ranking [(item, strength)] strongest first, with sub-floor items forgotten; osteogenesis remodels weights toward a load

assumes: values are finite; NaN/inf are rejected
estimates suffice: error is small in the body but larger in far tails with few points
for merging, shards were summarised with StreamHistogram (P2 summaries do not merge)

input.shape: a stream of numbers (one per line on stdin, or values fed in code), possibly too large to hold in memory, or several shards to merge

name: stream-quantiles
not_for: a small file that fits in memory where exact quantiles are cheap, or a CSV with several columns
output: running quantile estimates (median, p90, p99, any q) from P2 in 15 numbers, or a mergeable bounded histogram with exact min and max

assumes: the chart is square; only the ratio between axes carries over to wide charts
the slope is a least-squares line, so a V can show a small angle

input.shape: a price or metric series CSV or numbers list

name: stretch-axis
not_for: testing whether a trend is significant (it measures perception only)
output: per axis (tight, zero-based, padded) slope angle in degrees, max drawdown share of height, typical bar move; steepness ratio

assumes: modifiers are found by lexicon, -ly and adjective suffixes with no POS tagger - nouns like objective or metric and adjectives like red or flat are misread
the modifiers are decoration; in a technical note they often carry the fact (daily bars, negative return)
English prose sentences, numbers kept as facts

input.shape: a glowing result note or prose text

name: strip-adjectives
not_for: a technical spec where adjectives are the content (daily, adjusted, negative)
output: each sentence bare, per-sentence residual factual content ratio, overall ratio, most decorated sentence

assumes: preamble.md is the current version; prompts built from an older version fail the check
a scratch folder and the parent's open denials are supplied when emitting
forks inherit context and need no block

input.shape: a subagent prompt or work order saved as text (or the scratch folder and denials file to emit a block)

name: subagent-preamble
not_for: fork subagents, or prompts for a session that never runs on this Windows workspace
output: emit prints the SUBAGENT-PREAMBLE block; check says ok or names what is missing (exit 1); --hook exits 2 on an Agent prompt without the block

assumes: refs were fetched first (it follows local HEAD only and never fetches)
submodules sit within --depth of the root
each reader uses its own --state file and the clone path has not moved (state is keyed by absolute path)

input.shape: a root folder holding a git repo and nested repos or submodules, plus a state file of last-seen heads

name: submodule-since-last-look
not_for: remote branches nobody fetched, or files written but not committed (use recent-writes)
output: per repo NEW / MOVED (log since last sha) / REWRITTEN / same count; state updated only with --mark

assumes: requests follow the listed indirect forms; real questions ('can you see the file?') are also read as requests
complaints use the fixed problem-adjective list (slow, messy, stale, flaky); sarcasm is invisible

input.shape: a message with polite or indirect requests (could you, it would be nice if, I wonder whether)

name: subtext
not_for: deciding what Max ordered - a mapped directive is a reading, check with question-not-ruling
output: each indirect form with its class and the plain directive it implies (DO: ...) and softener count

assumes: the three estimates exist in the same units; a made-up p_success gives a made-up verdict (label each measured or guessed)
Max's wishes are recorded in still_wanted and asked_by_max; his own asks become ASK-MAX, never ABANDON
a point comparison with no variance is good enough; near-zero net value should be treated as ASK-MAX

input.shape: items.json: open work items each with remaining_cost, value_if_done, p_success (same units), superseded_by, still_wanted, asked_by_max

name: sunk-cost-check
not_for: a ledger with no cost/value estimates yet, or deleting code or branches (ABANDON means stop spending effort)
output: per item CONTINUE / ABANDON / ASK-MAX with the reason; exit 0 all CONTINUE, 1 something to abandon or ask, 2 bad input

assumes: tags are independent (naive-Bayes); correlated tags count twice
past outcomes used a comparable test, so a kill means the same thing across rows
the Beta(1,1) prior per tag is acceptable

input.shape: outcomes.jsonl of judged edges with tags and KILLED/SURVIVED plus candidates.jsonl of new ideas with tags

name: supernova-seed-priors
not_for: judging whether a candidate edge is real (a prior orders work, it is not evidence)
output: candidates sorted by prior survival with RE-TREAD / HEAVY-ASH / SEEDED / VIRGIN labels, per-tag deviations and kill causes

assumes: each line carries a timestamp in the named --field (JSONL) or as its first ISO stamp (text)
the writers' clocks agree within --slack
the log is meant to be written in time order - a log of backfilled or event-time rows breaks it by design

input.shape: an append-only log, JSONL with a time field or text lines with ISO timestamps

name: superposition
not_for: finding time GAPS in a log (sediment)
output: CONFORMABLE / INTRUDED / OVERTURNED with line numbers and displacement; exit 0 / 1 / 2

assumes: the threshold is the real safe capacity of the queue, backlog or risk budget
the trigger is observable as a yes/no event
release needs both excess and a trigger; excess alone keeps building

input.shape: a current level, a threshold (safe capacity) and a trigger flag, passed in code

name: supersaturation
not_for: detecting a shift after it happened (changepoint) or a quantity with no meaningful capacity
output: ratio level/threshold, zone under / saturated / supersaturated, primed flag and excess; will_release true only with excess and a trigger

assumes: the full population is normal and the cut is a hard threshold (skew or soft filters bias it)
about 30 or more values for the fit
the real cutoff is given; using the sample minimum understates truncation

input.shape: a list of kept values (series, JSON items with a column, optionally an alive/dead status field) cut off below a threshold

name: survivorship-view
not_for: recovering which items died (it estimates how many, not which)
output: visible fraction, estimated unseen count below the cutoff, and the survivor bias in the mean (or counted directly from a status field)

assumes: each sentence has one causal connective that matters (split at the first)
tense markers (was, -ed, will) are present; present-tense claims are graded open

input.shape: a because-story or note with causal connectives (because, since, due to, so, leads to, drives)

name: swap-cause-effect
not_for: testing causality in data - it questions the wording's arrow only
output: each causal claim reversed and graded time-locked / converse / open / plausible-reverse, with counts

assumes: each fault was planted once and every gate's catch was recorded; the matrix is built by plant-ledger, gate-registry or brood-parasite-check first
blank cells mean not run, not missed
the planted faults represent the real failure classes; escapes outside the planted set are invisible

input.shape: a planted-faults x gates catch matrix as CSV or JSONL (cells 1/0, caught/missed, killed/survived...; blank for not run)

name: swiss-cheese
not_for: a list of gates with no planted-fault results, or one test suite's mutant credit split (shapley-tests)
output: ESCAPES, SINGLE-POINT gates, REDUNDANT and CATCHES NOTHING gates, observed vs independent expected escapes (alignment), aligned pairs by miss-set Jaccard, greedy cover and VERDICT LAYERED / THIN / LEAKY (exit 0 only LAYERED)

assumes: each round's comparison is run on a fresh period so games are independent
the simulated accuracy at this n and number of rounds beats random pairings enough to be worth it
a draw within eps is a meaningful tie for the metric

input.shape: players.txt (one candidate per line), a games.jsonl history and per-round metric CSVs (player,value)

name: swiss-pairing
not_for: a short list small enough for a full round robin
output: round pairings with bye, game results, standings with Buchholz tie-breaks; simulate: Spearman and top-3 rate vs random and round robin; exit 1 no legal pairing

assumes: each partner has its own score measured both alone and coupled
the score is the same metric and scale before and after coupling
one measurement per condition is not noise - a small difference can flip the class

input.shape: four scores - A alone, B alone, A coupled, B coupled - or functions that compute them

name: symbiosis
not_for: a single combined score with no per-partner view
output: relationship (mutualism / commensalism / parasitism / competition), per-partner benefit, worth_coupling

assumes: the options really are tied; it ignores merit
each option has a stable identity (key) so every machine hashes the same thing
all parties agree on the seed

input.shape: a list of tied options (with an optional key for structured ones) and a seed, passed in code

name: symmetry-break
not_for: choosing among options that differ in quality, or deciding whether to act at all (quorum-sense)
output: one option, fixed for (options, seed), independent of order and unbiased across seeds

assumes: each sentence has a findable pivot verb (first auxiliary, known verb or -s/-ed word); long sentences swap ungrammatically
tense shifts follow a small irregular-verb table and plain rules

input.shape: English claim sentences, ideally short subject-verb-object

name: symmetry-variants
not_for: graded negation by evidence (use mirror-image) or flipping evaluative words (use polarity-flip)
output: per sentence the swap, flip and tense variants, labelled SWAP-INVARIANT or DIFFERENT CLAIM

assumes: quintile buckets are relative to the subject itself, not absolute
text channels are surface features (length, numbers...), not meaning
the subject is not code (refused)

input.shape: a numeric series (at least 5 values) or a text (at least 3 sentences); items heard column by column

name: synesthesia
not_for: any statistical claim - it re-renders, it measures nothing new
output: series: tone words per value, run-length phrase, leaps; text: a 5-number vector per sentence and the sentences that jump out

assumes: actions use one of about 80 common work verbs followed by a content word; unusual verbs are missed
a rule covers an action only when one rule sentence names both its verb and object; paraphrased rules do not match
without a rules file every repeated action is reported as unwritten

input.shape: a session log or text with one action per line, plus an optional rules file to compare against

name: tacit-knowledge
not_for: mining rules from Max's prompts (rule-miner) or a log of tool JSON with no plain-language action lines
output: TACIT lines: 'verb object' repeated N times with line numbers and no rule mentioning it, ranked by count

assumes: at least 8 points
the latest point is now and age bins are counted back from it
the oldest bin holds the leftover and may differ from the geometric size

input.shape: a numeric series of 8+ points, most recent last

name: telephoto-compression
not_for: deciding whether the near or far past matters more
output: geometric age bins with means and hidden ranges, share of variation hidden vs even-time bins, far-half share

assumes: markdown headings (else paragraphs, else equal chunks) mark the real sections
word frequency stands for gist - a section full of stop words gets a thin gist
for a series, segment means are an acceptable far view (everything inside a segment is hidden)

input.shape: a long text (or series)

name: telescope
not_for: a faithful prose summary, or seeing what the coarse view erased (zoom-ladder)
output: five theme words and one line per section with word share and two-word gist; for a series net drift, range position and segment means

assumes: tense is read from regex markers (-ed words are past; present is the default)
conditionals read as present and quoted speech is not separated
one sentence or one plan step is one claim

input.shape: a plan, pitch or report in English prose

name: tense-sort
not_for: judging whether a forecast is right (calibration-check) or non-English text
output: counts of past fact, present state and future forecast, and flagged sentences: forecast rests on a past result, certain forecast, mixed past and future

assumes: terms-reader already ruled on each source and its terms text was saved under terms/
the adapter calls require() first and its hosts appear as literal strings the scan can find
the deny list names every banned source (e.g. kraken)

input.shape: a terms.lock of source verdicts with saved terms text, plus adapter code folders to scan

name: terms-gate
not_for: reading or judging the terms themselves (use terms-reader)
output: require raises TermsRefused; verify prints OK / TERMS-CHANGED / TERMS-MISSING per source; scan prints UNLOCKED-HOST / REFUSED-HOST / DENIED-NAME with file:line

assumes: one use-case sentence was written before reading and given to every reader
readings use the exact verdict words (ALLOWED, ALLOWED WITH LIMITS (...), NOT ALLOWED, FORBIDDEN, UNCLEAR (...), NOT READ, CONFIRMED)
the reading came from the terms pages themselves - the agent never fetches data

input.shape: TERMS_READING_<VENDOR>_<date>.md files in the fixed format (use case line, Q sections with VERDICT lines, verbatim quote and URL)

name: terms-reader
not_for: free-prose notes about a vendor - they fail the format by design
output: exit 0 well-formed and nothing blocks; 1 MALFORMED (QUALIFIED_ALLOWED, BAD_VERDICT, NO_QUOTE, NO_URL, NO_USE_CASE); 3 a NOT ALLOWED / FORBIDDEN / NOT READ blocker for Max

assumes: the indicator is ported and verified bar-for-bar; an unverified port is not used
--tries counts every condition tried so far, so the charged p is honest
forward returns are aligned with the condition day without look-ahead and a realistic round-trip cost is given

input.shape: data.json {returns: forward return per day, condition: true/false per day}, or a stock_scan.py --when condition on ported indicators

name: test-a-condition
not_for: a strategy with position sizing and exits (backtest-verdict) or a condition on an unported indicator
output: trades, conditional mean vs buy-any-day baseline, permutation p, charged p (Sidak), mean after cost, edge in each half; verdict TOO FEW / NO EDGE / LEAD (never tradable)

assumes: a derivation is a hand-line comment near the expected value; derivations kept elsewhere are not seen
magic means non-round floats and counts >= 10; round values like 0.25 are trusted
it is run on NEW tests; old suites produce a backlog of mostly-correct numbers

input.shape: pytest test files (test_*.py) with asserted expected values

name: test-expectation-oracle
not_for: proving an expected value is correct (it only finds ones nobody derived)
output: X-MAGIC (expected value with no hand line) and X-TAUTOLOGY (call-free self comparison) lines per test file

assumes: the tests.json format round-trips exactly (indent, ensure_ascii, newline)
pytest can collect the test file
tv-core's testreg is the first choice inside a tv-* project

input.shape: a project's tests.json and its pytest test files

name: tests-json-registrar
not_for: deleting tests.json entries (retire with a reason)
output: collected / new / already counts; rename with history kept; stale list; exit 0 / 1 / 2

assumes: each case has a book or paper source with a page / table / eq. locator (else REFUSED)
the function signature fits the case inputs (adapt with a lambda)
tolerance is no tighter than the printed precision, and registry values entered from memory are checked against the book once

input.shape: a numeric python function plus registry case ids, each with inputs, a published value, a tolerance and a sourced locator

name: textbook-handshake
not_for: proving a tool right on every input (only the cases tried), or a quantity with no published reference value
output: PASS / FAIL (with deviation) / REFUSED / ERROR per case and trusted() True only when every requested case passes

assumes: roughness is scale-free: a quiet choppy stretch scores like a violent one (use envelope-view or ewma-vol for size)
windows are long enough (default n/6, at least 6); one window's label is weak evidence

input.shape: a price or value series file

name: texture-view
not_for: forecasting choppiness (it describes the past)
output: per half-overlapping window roughness, high-frequency share and a smooth / grainy / rough label, plus the overall value

assumes: the outcome field's sign means win/loss; zero outcomes are skipped
there are at least --min-group pairs after losses and after wins (default 3)
the size field is what the decision-maker chose, not something set by an external rule

input.shape: a JSONL of decisions in time order (or with --time-field), each with a signed outcome and the size of the action taken

name: tilt-meter
not_for: a record where a sizing rule (vol-targeting) legitimately shrinks size after losses - check the rule before calling it tilt
output: STEADY (exit 0) or TILT-UP / TILT-DOWN (exit 1) with permutation p, mean next size after a loss vs after a win and the ratio

assumes: the question is whether the endpoints carry the result; outliers inside the middle are not tested
the 50% endpoint-share threshold is a fixed rule of thumb with no p-value
the trim fraction (default 0.15) suits the series length

input.shape: a numeric series such as an equity curve or price path behind a trend or return claim

name: tilt-shift
not_for: uncertainty intervals (bootstrap-ci) or a series with no trend claim
output: slope and mean with ends trimmed or blurred vs whole, flips, end share and ENDPOINT-DEPENDENT or robust

assumes: anything shorter than a frame is hidden and turning points are smoothed (try two frame counts)

not_for: a single strategy's significance - use deflated-sharpe / hac-forward
output: raw winner -> expected (shrunk) value with haircut %, P(edge > 0), tau vs typical se, NO DETECTABLE SPREAD when differences are noise, and a table per candidate

assumes: the parents have vowel-group seams; the vowel-seam rule reaches many but not all classic portmanteaus
offspring are candidates to pick from, not guaranteed real words; the pronounceability gate is heuristic
phrase children must blend words from both parents and may be ungrammatical

input.shape: two parent words (or two phrases with phrase_sex, or two numbers with number_sex) given on the command line

name: word-sex
not_for: finding an existing word or editing prose; it generates candidates only
output: ranked pronounceable novel offspring with scores; phrase_sex gives blended phrase children; number_sex gives the mediant, means and digit crossovers

assumes: assumptions are read from a short fixed list of AST patterns (iterated, opened, divided, indexed args, globals); library type expectations and keyword-only args are missed
plan mode knows about 15 common verbs; others get only the hand-off check

input.shape: one Python source file, or a plan.txt of steps (--kind plan)

name: worms-eye
not_for: a whole multi-module repo (calls across modules are not followed)
output: functions ordered leaves first, each with its assumptions and the caller that must honour them

assumes: exactly one writer appends to the log (no locking inside)
the log is in its own seq TAB crc32 TAB json format and small enough to replay in memory (compact before hundreds of MB)
damage is accidental - CRC32 catches bit-rot and torn writes, not a deliberate rewrite

input.shape: a WAL file of seq TAB crc32 TAB canonical-json lines

name: write-ahead-log
not_for: tamper evidence on a ledger someone may edit (blockchain-decisions, chain-fork-guard) or a log written by several processes
output: replayed records to stdout, summary to stderr (good count, corrupt_at, tail_bad, torn, gaps); CorruptionError on mid-log damage, SequenceGapError on gaps

assumes: write paths resolve from literals, f-strings or one-hop names; about half stay UNRESOLVED and are neither cleared nor flagged
readers are in python code; humans, git, scheduled tasks or other tools that read a file are invisible
files are matched by basename, so two same-named files in different folders look like one

input.shape: a python code tree that appends or writes files (logs, ledgers, outputs)

name: write-only-log
not_for: deciding to delete a log (no reader in code is not no reader), or non-python trees
output: WRITE-ONLY and MENTIONED rows with size on disk (--all adds READ, UNRESOLVED, TEMP); --json

assumes: a dead pid says nothing about staleness; a force needs a quoted OK from the holder or Max
the claim's exit code is checked before any write (never chained with ;)
pen_history reads the real chain under $AUTOTRADE_ROOT or the passed --repo

input.shape: the shared writer chain (shared/writer.chain.jsonl) of pen claims and releases, plus saved #41 comments for a force gate

name: writer-pen
not_for: a repo with only one session writing (no coordination is needed)
output: pen_history: HELD / FREE, holder, typical hold, LONG and FORCED lines; pen_force_gate: ALLOW / REFUSED / FREE (exit 0 / 1 / 3); pen_lock refuses a second claim or an unapproved force

assumes: support is written with explicit connectors; implicit support between sentences is invisible
'since' is read as a reason even in its time sense

input.shape: an argument in prose with explicit connectors (because, so, therefore)

name: x-ray
not_for: judging whether the supports are true - pair with evidence-only or falsifier-view
output: a claim tree (CLAIM with its 'because' supports nested) and the list of unsupported top claims

assumes: counter-evidence must be on the same page; a claim with none stays UNTESTED
sentences are paired by shared words, which can pair sentences that share a word but not a subject
amplification swaps known quantifiers and modals only

input.shape: a memo, thesis or rule-of-thumb text with at least 2 claims, some softened (usually, most, may, small)

name: zealot-eye
not_for: a single claim or a text with no softened claims; testing against outside data
output: each claim's absolutist form with the swaps made, and BREAKS lines naming the sentence that contradicts it, or UNTESTED

assumes: block averages, not OHLC resampling, so drawdowns and spikes fade by construction
the pattern of interest is in the fixed feature set (trend sign, reversals, drawdown, spike, high/low quarter)

input.shape: one numeric series, long enough for several power-of-two block-average levels

name: zoom-ladder
not_for: a pattern outside the fixed feature set
output: per level features, which hold at every scale, which appear raw only or vanish at each rung

assumes: the code is Python and hands work to a pool or threads (ProcessPoolExecutor, multiprocessing, threading)
the shared target is a database or file several workers write
the job can be run on a copy of real-size data

input.shape: a source tree; then the job's own command on a full-size copy of its data

name: caste-split
not_for: workers that each write only their own private file; single-process code
output: CANDIDATE workers that write (file:line, the writes); then a compute()/apply() split with one writer, proved identical and measured at full size
